cues.en: Norman: 1984, the Cold War raged between two superpowers:

cues.zh: 美国和苏联。

cues.zh: 重大的经济和政治分歧让这两个曾经的盟友长期处于紧张状态。
cues.en: Major economic and political differences created a constant state of tension between the former allies.

cues.zh: Apple 发布了备受期待的 Macintosh 个人电脑；

cues.zh: 洛杉矶举办了1984年夏季奥运会；

cues.zh: 两部大片登陆影院：《捉鬼敢死队》和《小精灵》；
cues.en: two major blockbusters hit theaters: "Ghostbusters" and "Gremlins";

cues.en: The nation grew and prospered, socially and economically.

cues.zh: 但共产主义苏联的情况截然不同：
cues.en: But the Communist Soviet Union was a stark contrast:

cues.zh: 石油是该国主要出口产品之一，其价格下跌；

cues.zh: 该国以“反苏歇斯底里”为由抵制了1984年夏季奥运会；

cues.zh: 总书记康斯坦丁·契尔年科病入膏肓；

cues.zh: 米哈伊尔·戈尔巴乔夫在一旁伺机而动；

cues.zh: 该国与阿富汗的冲突已持续五年；
cues.en: the country was five years into a conflict with Afghanistan;

cues.zh: 民众日益不满，手头拮据；
cues.en: citizens grew frustrated and had little money;

cues.zh: 政府推行全面改革，以根除异见、恢复秩序。
cues.en: the government enacted sweeping reforms to eradicate dissent and restore order.

cues.zh: 这两个国家可谓泾渭分明，
cues.en: The two nations couldn't have been more divided,

cues.zh: 但就在那个夏天，苏联的一位程序员创造出了特别的东西：
cues.en: but that summer, a computer programmer in the Soviet Union created something special:

cues.zh: 那是一款益智游戏，它席卷了电子游戏行业，并帮助打破了两个超级大国之间的界限。
cues.en: It was a puzzle game that took the video game industry by storm and helped break the boundaries between the two superpowers.

cues.zh: Alexey Leonidovich Pajitnov 于1956年3月14日出生在莫斯科。
cues.en: Alexey Leonidovich Pajitnov was born on March 14th, 1956 in Moscow.

cues.zh: 他的母亲是一名记者，报道电影——这在苏联是一种颇有争议的艺术形式。
cues.en: His mother was a journalist who reported on cinema, a somewhat controversial art form in the Soviet Union.

cues.zh: 他的父亲是一位哲学家、作家，也是共产主义政权的异见者。
cues.en: His father was a philosopher, a writer and a dissident of the communist regime.

cues.zh: Pajitnov 11岁时，父母离婚了。
cues.en: When Pajitnov was 11, his parents divorced.

cues.zh: 从那以后，他和母亲独自住在一间一居室的公寓里。
cues.en: From then on, he and his mother lived alone in a one-bedroom apartment.

cues.zh: 但和母亲相处的时光让他接触到了流行文化。
cues.en: But their time together introduced him to pop culture.

cues.zh: 作为记者，他的母亲经常参加莫斯科国际电影节。
cues.en: As a writer, his mother regularly attended the Moscow International Film Festival.

cues.zh: 有时她会带上年幼的 Alexey，让他接触来自世界各地的电影。
cues.en: Sometimes she brought young Alexey along and introduced him to films from around the world.

cues.zh: 他喜欢 James Bond。
cues.en: He loved James Bond.

cues.zh: 他也喜欢数学谜题和桌游，这是苏联孩子们为数不多能接触到的娱乐形式之一。
cues.en: He also loved math puzzles and board games, one of the few forms of entertainment available to children of the Soviet Union.

cues.zh: 他最喜欢的游戏之一是五格骨牌。
cues.en: One of his favorites was Pentominoes.

cues.zh: 游戏目标是把 12 块各由五个方块组成的独特拼图拼成一个矩形。
cues.en: The goal of the game is to arrange 12 unique puzzle pieces, consisting of five blocks, each into a rectangle.

cues.zh: 作为 60 年代的孩子，帕基特诺夫见证了美国和苏联之间的太空探索竞赛。
cues.en: As a child in the 60's, Pajitnov witnessed the competition of space exploration between the United States and the Soviet Union.

cues.zh: 苏联招募科学家和工程师以取得优势。
cues.en: The USSR recruited scientists and engineers to give them an advantage.

cues.zh: 他们希望通过展示最新技术来吸引孩子们进入这一领域。
cues.en: They hoped to draw children into the field by showing off the latest technology.

cues.zh: 结果，17 岁的帕基特诺夫接触到了计算机。
cues.en: As a result, 17 year-old Pajitnov was introduced to the computer.

cues.zh: 这给他留下了深刻的印象。
cues.en: It left a lasting impression on him.

cues.zh: 他考入莫斯科航空学院，在那里获得了应用数学硕士学位。
cues.en: He enrolled at the Moscow Institute of Aviation, where he earned his Master's Degree in Applied Mathematics.

cues.zh: 毕业后，帕基特诺夫加入了莫斯科著名的俄罗斯科学院，在多罗尼岑计算中心获得了一个研究职位。
cues.en: After graduating, Pajitnov joined the famous Russian Academy of Sciences in Moscow, where he landed a research position in the Dorodnicyn Computing Center.

cues.zh: 但计算中心并不算走在技术前沿。
cues.en: But the Computing Center wasn't exactly at the forefront of technology.

cues.zh: 所有员工共用同一台房间大小的大型机。
cues.en: All employees used the same, room-sized mainframe computer.

cues.zh: 工作条件也不理想。帕基特诺夫和另外三名研究员共用一张办公桌。
cues.en: Work conditions weren't ideal either. Pajitnov shared his desk with three other researchers.

cues.zh: 他几乎每天都遵循同样的作息：早上7:30到8:00之间起床，早餐吃香肠、鸡蛋和农家干酪，办些杂事，然后10:00前到计算中心。
cues.en: He followed the same routine almost every day: wake up between 7:30 and 8:00 am, eat a breakfast of sausage, eggs and cottage cheese, run some errands, then arrive at the computing center by 10:00 am.

cues.zh: 他一直工作到午夜，这让他晚上有一些独处的时间。
cues.en: He worked until midnight, which gave him some alone time in the evenings.

cues.zh: 后来，帕基特诺夫和几位员工得到了升级：每人一台自己的 Electronica 60 计算机工作站。
cues.en: Eventually, Pajitnov and a few other employees got an upgrade: their own personal Electronica 60 Computer Workstation.

cues.zh: 相比巨型大型机，这是巨大的升级。
cues.en: It was a huge upgrade over the giant mainframe computers.

cues.zh: 但对现代世界的其他地方来说，它已经老掉牙了。
cues.en: But to the rest of the modern world, it was ancient.

cues.zh: Electronica 60 是 LSI 11 计算机的克隆机，而 LSI 11 是九年前推出的系统。
cues.en: The Electronica 60 was a clone of the LSI 11 Computer, a system that came out nine years prior.

cues.zh: 显示器不显示任何图形，只有字母数字字符。
cues.en: The display didn't show any graphics, only alphanumeric characters.

cues.zh: Pajitnov 从事人工智能程序和语音识别软件的开发；
cues.en: Pajitnov worked on artificial intelligence programs and speech recognition software;

cues.zh: 后者引起了俄罗斯安全总局克格勃的注意。
cues.en: the latter caught the attention of the KGB, Russia's head Security Agency.

cues.zh: 他们希望它能记录电话通话。
cues.en: They hoped it could record phone conversations.

cues.zh: 但到了晚上，Pajitnov 和其他几位研究员就能独占这些计算机，做自己的副业项目。
cues.en: But in the evenings, Pajitnov and a few other researchers had the computers to themselves, to work on their own side projects.

cues.zh: 有一位程序员痴迷于 Pac-Man，那是少数几款越过铁幕传进来的街机游戏之一。
cues.en: One programmer was obsessed with Pac-Man, one of the few arcade games to make its way past the Iron Curtain.

cues.zh: 他花了几个小时试图逆向工程它。
cues.en: He spent hours trying to reverse-engineer it.

cues.zh: 还有 Dmitry Pavlovsky，一位研究员同事兼朋友，他在计算中心里那台巨大的大型机上编写了好几款游戏。
cues.en: There was also Dmitry Pavlovsky, a fellow researcher and friend who programmed several games on the giant mainframe computer stored away in the computing center.

cues.zh: 还有一位16岁的编程天才，名叫Vadim Gerasimov。
cues.en: There was also a 16 year old programming prodigy, named Vadim Gerasimov.

cues.zh: 他给计算机科学老师留下了深刻印象，随后被带到计算中心，进一步学习编程并协助项目。
cues.en: After impressing his computer science teacher, he was brought to the Computing Center to learn more about programming and assist with projects.

cues.zh: Pavlovsky把Gerasimov介绍给了Alexey Pajitnov。
cues.en: Pavlovsky introduced Gerasimov to Alexey Pajitnov.

cues.zh: 三人都对电脑游戏和编程充满热爱，于是组建了团队，晚上一起头脑风暴游戏创意。
cues.en: The trio shared a love of computer games and programming, so they formed a team and brainstormed game ideas in the evenings.

cues.zh: 他们希望能把游戏打包，甚至卖出去，这在苏联是极其困难的事。
cues.en: They hoped to package the games and possibly sell them, an extremely difficult endeavor in the Soviet Union.

cues.zh: Pajitnov坐在桌前，苦思冥想直到深夜。
cues.en: Pajitnov sat at his desk late into the night, brainstorming.

cues.zh: 他回想起童年时光，那时他花了好几个小时玩五格骨牌。
cues.en: He thought back to his childhood, when he spent hours playing Pentominoes.

cues.zh: 一定有办法把这种体验搬到电脑上。
cues.en: Surely there was a way to translate this experience to the computer.

cues.zh: Pajitnov对标准五格骨牌游戏做了调整，以适应他那台过时的硬件。
cues.en: Pajitnov made adjustments to the standard Pentomino game to accommodate for his outdated hardware.

cues.zh: 他把五个方块形状缩减到四个，把拼块数量从12块减少到7块。
cues.en: He cut the five block shapes down to four, which reduced the number of pieces from 12 to 7.

cues.zh: 六天后，帕基特诺夫完成了他的第一个版本。
cues.en: In six days, Pajitnov completed his first version.

cues.zh: 他给它起名叫“基因工程”。
cues.en: He named it "Genetic Engineering."

cues.zh: 目标很简单，把拼块排列到刚好装进一个盒子里。
cues.en: The goal was simple, arrange the pieces until they fit into a box.

cues.zh: 它成功了，但只有一个问题：
cues.en: It worked, but there was just one problem:

cues.zh: 它很无聊。
cues.en: it was boring.

cues.zh: 一旦玩家想出了解法，就没有理由再玩一遍。
cues.en: Once a player figured out the solution, they had no reason to play again.

cues.zh: 游戏需要挑战并吸引玩家。
cues.en: The game needed to challenge and engage the player.

cues.zh: 于是帕基特诺夫让游戏变得更紧张刺激。
cues.en: So Pajitnov made the game more hectic.

cues.zh: 他把游戏区域缩小到屏幕中央，让拼块不断下落。
cues.en: He narrowed the playing field to the center of the screen and had the pieces fall constantly.

cues.zh: 它确实更吸引人、节奏更快了，但这带来了一个新问题：
cues.en: It was definitely more engaging and fast-paced, but that created a new problem:

cues.zh: 如果你没能填满一行，它会留在屏幕上。
cues.en: If you failed to complete a row, it stayed on the screen.

cues.zh: 如果你填满了一行，它也还是留在屏幕上。
cues.en: If you completed a row, it stayed on the screen too.

cues.zh: 玩起来不够爽，游戏结束得太快了。
cues.en: It wasn't satisfying and the game ended too quickly.

cues.zh: Pajitnov的下一次改动让游戏变得令人上瘾。
cues.en: Pajitnov's next modification made the game addictive.

cues.zh: 玩家一旦填满一整行，这一行就会消失。
cues.en: As soon as the player filled in an entire row, it disappeared.

cues.zh: 游戏有可能永远进行下去，而把拼图块拼合在一起本身就是一种令人满足的奖励。
cues.en: The game could potentially last forever and fitting the puzzle pieces together was a satisfying reward.

cues.zh: 突然间，他玩自己的新游戏停不下来了。他甚至在工作时间也玩，声称自己在“调试软件”。
cues.en: Suddenly, he couldn't stop playing his new game. He even played during work hours, claiming to be "debugging software."

cues.zh: 这款游戏天生就令人上瘾，不需要任何教程或说明。
cues.en: The game was naturally addictive and didn't require any sort of tutorial or explanation.

cues.zh: Pajitnov把游戏命名为“Tetris”，将希腊语中表示“四”的“tetra”与他最喜欢的运动网球（tennis）组合在一起。
cues.en: Pajitnov named the game "Tetris", combining the Greek word "tetra" meaning four with his favorite sport, tennis.

cues.zh: 它只有基础的计分系统，没有声音，也没有额外关卡。
cues.en: It had a basic scoring system, no sound and no extra levels.

cues.zh: 但它令人上瘾，而且无疑是三人电脑游戏合集里最好的一款。
cues.en: But it was addictive and easily the best game in the trio's computer game package.

cues.zh: 但没人想过俄罗斯方块能走出多罗尼岑计算中心的大楼。
cues.en: But no one ever imagined Tetris would make it outside the halls of the Dorodnicyn Computing Center.

cues.zh: 它只能在过时的 Electronica 60 计算机上运行。
cues.en: It only worked on the outdated Electronica 60 Computer.

cues.zh: 俄罗斯方块在俄罗斯科学院收获了一小群狂热粉丝。
cues.en: Tetris gained a small cult following at the Russian Academy of Sciences.

cues.zh: 帕基特诺夫想扩大受众，但唯一的办法就是把游戏移植到更普及的平台上，也就是 IBM PC。
cues.en: Pajitnov wanted to expand his audience, but the only way to do that was to program the game for a more commonly available platform, the IBM PC.

cues.zh: 他找到了 16 岁的天才少年瓦季姆·格拉西莫夫，问他能否帮忙。
cues.en: He approached the 16 year old whiz kid, Vadim Gerasimov and asked if he could assist.

cues.zh: 这任务有点难度；
cues.en: It would be a somewhat difficult task;

cues.zh: 格拉西莫夫需要在一台他从未用过的电脑上重写整个程序。
cues.en: Gerasimov needed to rewrite the entire program on a computer he'd never used before.

cues.zh: 但仅仅几天，格拉西莫夫就做出了可用的原型。
cues.en: But in only a few days, Gerasimov had a working prototype.

cues.zh: 几周后，他就准备好了功能完整、兼容性广泛的版本。
cues.en: He had a fully functional, widely compatible version ready in a few weeks.

cues.zh: 他为俄罗斯方块加入了颜色、多个关卡，还有保存最高分的功能。
cues.en: He added color to the Tetrominoes, multiple levels, plus the ability to save your high score.

cues.zh: 俄罗斯方块比以往任何时候都更让人上瘾。
cues.en: Tetris was more addictive than ever before.

cues.zh: 然而，想靠他们的游戏合集赚钱的梦想却在破灭：
cues.en: However, the dream of selling their collection of games was falling apart:

cues.zh: 在共产主义的苏联，创业本就罕见，更别提软件生意了。
cues.en: Starting a business, let alone a software business, was highly unusual in communist Soviet Union.

cues.zh: 而且，他们是在俄罗斯科学院做出俄罗斯方块的，严格来说这游戏算是政府财产。
cues.en: Plus, they made Tetris at the Russian Academy of Sciences, which technically made the game government property.

cues.zh: Pajtinov、Pavlovsky 和 Gerasimov 不想让自己的心血白费。
cues.en: Pajtinov, Pavlovsky and Gerasimov didn't want to see their hard work go to waste.

cues.zh: 他们给游戏合集取名“Computer FunFair”，并制作了副本，分发给任何感兴趣的人。
cues.en: They named their collection of games "Computer FunFair" and made copies, which they distributed to whoever was interested.

cues.zh: 其中一个人就是 Vladimir Pokhilko，他是 Alexey Pajitnov 的朋友，也是莫斯科医疗中心的临床心理学家。
cues.en: One such person was Vladimir Pokhilko, Alexey Pajitnov's friend and a clinical psychologist at the Moscow Medical Center.

cues.zh: 当他在工作站上打开俄罗斯方块时，立刻意识到这款游戏有多让人上瘾。
cues.en: When he fired up Tetris at his workstation, he immediately recognized the addictive nature of the game.

cues.zh: 随着一行行方块消失，玩家会感到情绪高涨，越玩越想玩。
cues.en: As rows of blocks disappeared, it gave the player an emotional high, fueling them to keep playing.

cues.zh: 波希爾科给同事们拷贝了这款游戏。
cues.en: Pokhilko made copies of the game for his fellow employees.

cues.zh: 很快，整个心理学系都迷上了它。
cues.en: Soon, the entire psychology department was hooked.

cues.zh: 波希爾科担心游戏会影响工作，于是销毁了医疗中心里的每一份拷贝。
cues.en: Pokhilko feared the game would interfere with their work, so he destroyed every copy in the medical center.

cues.zh: 但这款游戏又悄悄回来了。
cues.en: But the game found its way back.

cues.zh: 波希爾科没有一味抵制，而是认为这款游戏可以用来研究成瘾。
cues.en: Rather than fight it, Pokhilko thought the game could be useful in studying addiction.

cues.zh: 帕基特诺夫和格拉西莫夫专门为莫斯科医疗中心开发了一个独特的双人版本。
cues.en: A unique two-player version was developed specifically for the Moscow Medical Center by Pajitnov and Gerasimov.

cues.zh: 到1986年，俄罗斯方块如野火般传遍了整个苏联。
cues.en: By 1986, Tetris spread like wildfire throughout the Soviet Union.

cues.zh: 几乎任何能接触到 IBM PC 的人都玩过某种形式的这款游戏。
cues.en: Almost anyone with access to an IBM PC had some form of the game.

cues.zh: 帕基特诺夫没赚到一分钱，但他为这款游戏的流行感到兴奋。但这仅仅是开始。
cues.en: Pajitnov didn't make a penny, but he was excited about the popularity of the game. But it was only the beginning.

cues.zh: 最终，俄罗斯方块走出了苏联，引发了一场围绕这款益智游戏牟利的史诗级争夺战。
cues.en: Eventually, Tetris made its way outside the Soviet Union, which ignited an epic battle to cash in on the puzzle game.

cues.zh: 凭借简单又令人上瘾的玩法机制，俄罗斯方块占据了苏联工人的闲暇时间。
cues.en: With its simple and addictive gameplay mechanics, Tetris took over the free time of Soviet workers.

cues.zh: 其中一个人就是阿列克谢·帕基特诺夫的老板。
cues.en: One such person was Alexey Pajitnov's boss.

cues.zh: 他把一份拷贝分享给了匈牙利布达佩斯 SCKI 计算机科学研究所的一些同事。
cues.en: He shared a copy with some colleagues at the SCKI Institute of Computer Science in Budapest, Hungary.

cues.zh: 他们爱不释手。
cues.en: They loved it.

cues.zh: 研究所的一些学生甚至把游戏移植到了 Commodore 64 和 Apple II 上，这是西方世界两款流行的家用电脑。
cues.en: Some students at the Institute even ported the game to the Commodore 64 and Apple II, two popular home computers in the Western world.

cues.zh: 就这样，俄罗斯方块正式越过了铁幕。
cues.en: With that, Tetris officially crossed the Iron Curtain.

cues.zh: 某种意义上，匈牙利是西方世界与苏联生活最紧密的联系。
cues.en: In a sense, Hungary was the Western world's closest connection to Soviet life.

cues.zh: 它处于共产党统治之下，但在1956年革命之后，匈牙利政府推行了重大经济改革，打造出更开放的自由市场。
cues.en: It was under Communist rule, but after the 1956 Revolution, the Hungarian government passed major economic reforms to create a more open free-market.

cues.zh: 匈牙利最受欢迎的出口产品之一是魔方，由Erno Rubik于1974年发明。
cues.en: One of Hungary's most popular exports was the Rubik's Cube, created by Erno Rubik in 1974.

cues.zh: 对于想把东方产品授权给西方受众的商人来说，匈牙利是必去之地。
cues.en: Hungary was the place to go for business people looking to license Eastern products to Western audiences.

cues.zh: 其中一位商人是Robert Stein，英国软件公司Andromeda Software的老板。
cues.en: One such businessman was Robert Stein, owner of the British software company Andromeda Software.

cues.zh: 在80年代销售计算机硬件之后，Stein转向了利润丰厚得多的生意：卖软件。
cues.en: After selling computer hardware in the 80s, Stein switched to a much more profitable business: selling software.

cues.zh: 但他没有在英国寻找潜在的新游戏，而是在祖国匈牙利找到了人才。
cues.en: But rather than look for potential new games in the UK, he found his talent in his native country of Hungary.

cues.zh: 他的商业模式很简单：找一款游戏，卖给西方的发行商，然后从销售中抽取版税。
cues.en: His business model was simple: find a game, sell it to a publisher in the West, and collect royalties on the sales.

cues.zh: Stein经常去SCKI计算机科学研究所寻找新游戏，1986年，他注意到有人在计算机实验室的角落里玩一款游戏。
cues.en: Stein frequently visited the SCKI Institute of Computer Science for new titles, and in 1986, he noticed someone playing a game in the corner of the computer lab.

cues.zh: 那就是Tetris。
cues.en: It was Tetris.

cues.zh: “这到底是什么玩意儿？”他问道。
cues.en: "What the hell is this?" he asked.

cues.zh: “哦，就是个游戏而已，”一名员工回答道。
cues.en: "Oh, it's just a game," an employee replied.

cues.zh: Stein来了兴趣，亲自试玩了一下。
cues.en: Intrigued, Stein tried the game for himself.

cues.zh: 他并不是游戏玩家，但他玩Tetris停不下来。
cues.en: He wasn't a gamer, but he couldn't stop playing Tetris.

cues.zh: 这游戏必定大卖。
cues.en: It was a surefire hit.

cues.zh: 他立刻去找研究所所长询问授权事宜。
cues.en: He immediately went to the director of the Institute and inquired about licensing.

cues.zh: 但所长不好意思地承认，这游戏不是他们的。
cues.en: But the director sheepishly admitted that the game wasn't theirs.

cues.zh: 如果Stein想获得Tetris的授权，他得和苏联谈交易，但这事说起来容易做起来难。
cues.en: If Stein wanted to license Tetris, he would have to make a deal with the Soviet Union, but that was easier said than done.

cues.zh: 当时俄罗斯的经济仍然非常封闭。
cues.en: Russia's economy was still very closed off.

cues.zh: 斯坦因直接飞到莫斯科谈成交易的可能性微乎其微。
cues.en: The chances of Stein simply flying to Moscow and brokering a deal was slim to none.

cues.zh: 但这位总监确实有一条沟通渠道：他有俄罗斯科学院电传机的号码。
cues.en: But the director did have one line of communication: he had the number to the Russian Academy of Sciences' Telex machine.

cues.zh: 斯坦因发了一封电传，说他想获得Tetris的版权。
cues.en: Stein sent a Telex message stating that he wanted to acquire the rights to Tetris.

cues.zh: 这条消息被转给了创作者Alexey Pajitnov。
cues.en: The message was forwarded to the creator, Alexey Pajitnov.

cues.zh: Pajitnov震惊了。
cues.en: Pajitnov was shocked.

cues.zh: 他早已放弃了卖软件的想法。
cues.en: He'd given up the idea of selling software.

cues.zh: 现在，他收到了一份关于Tetris版权的书面报价，但他必须谨慎。
cues.en: Now, he had an offer in writing for the rights to Tetris, but he had to be cautious.

cues.zh: 他做出了Tetris，但他无权就这款游戏的版权进行谈判。
cues.en: He made Tetris, but he had no authority to negotiate for the rights to the game.

cues.zh: “我们不能为个人利益做任何事，”他说。
cues.en: "We can do nothing for personal gain," he said.

cues.zh: 不过，能让一款游戏出版，将是一项巨大的成就。
cues.en: It would, however, be a huge accomplishment to have a game published.

cues.zh: 经过几周的翻译和正式授权，帕基特诺夫发出了以下回复：
cues.en: After several weeks of getting translations and the proper authorization, Pajitnov sent the following reply:

cues.zh: “是的，我们感兴趣。我们愿意达成这笔交易。”
cues.en: "Yes, we are interested. We would like to have this deal."

cues.zh: 对帕基特诺夫来说，这是一种表达“我们再深入谈谈”的方式。
cues.en: For Pajitnov, it was a way of saying, "Let's talk more about this."

cues.zh: 他不想做出承诺，因为害怕受到政府的纪律处分，但他也不想关上大门。
cues.en: He didn't want to commit for fear of discipline from his government, but he didn't want to shut the door, either.

cues.zh: 但在罗伯特·斯坦看来，这是一项口头协议。
cues.en: But to Robert Stein, it was a verbal agreement.

cues.zh: 据他所知，Andromeda Software可以为Tetris找到买家。
cues.en: As far as he knew, Andromeda Software could find a buyer for Tetris.

cues.zh: 斯坦立即去找了他在英国的常合作出版商之一，Mirrorsoft。
cues.en: Stein immediately went to one of his go-to publishers in the UK, Mirrorsoft.

cues.zh: Mirrorsoft是庞大的Maxwell Communications Corporation的软件部门。
cues.en: Mirrorsoft was the software division of the massive Maxwell Communications Corporation.

cues.zh: Maxwell Corporation由罗伯特·麦克斯韦创立，他是一位获得勋章的二战老兵和前国会议员，该公司拥有几家报纸、杂志，甚至还有一家足球俱乐部。
cues.en: Founded by Robert Maxwell, a decorated World War 2 veteran and former member of Parliament, the Maxwell Corporation owned several newspapers magazines and even a soccer club.

cues.zh: Mirrorsoft是一家财力雄厚的大型发行商。
cues.en: Mirrorsoft was a big publisher with strong financial backing.

cues.zh: Stein安排与Mirrorsoft联合创始人Jim Mackonochie会面。
cues.en: Stein set up a meeting with Mirrorsoft co-founder Jim Mackonochie.

cues.zh: 他看了看俄罗斯方块，没当回事，就把它转给了Mirrorsoft的技术部门。
cues.en: He took a look at Tetris, thought nothing of it, and passed it off to Mirrorsoft's technical department.

cues.zh: 几周后，Mackonochie在午休时溜达到技术部门，发现大家都围在一起玩俄罗斯方块。
cues.en: Several weeks later, Mackonochie wandered down to the technical department during a lunch break and noticed everyone huddled around playing Tetris.

cues.zh: 他觉得自己也该玩玩这个游戏。
cues.en: He figured he should play the game himself.

cues.zh: 他把它带回家，很快Mackonochie、他妻子和孩子们都迷上了。
cues.en: He took it home, and soon Mackonochie, his wife, and their children were hooked.

cues.zh: 除了Mirrorsoft，Maxwell Corporation在美国还有另一家软件公司Spectrum HoloByte。
cues.en: Along with Mirrorsoft, Maxwell Corporation had another software company in the United States, Spectrum HoloByte.

cues.zh: Mirrorsoft和Spectrum HoloByte合作得很好，经常共享游戏作品，并在各自区域发行游戏。
cues.en: Mirrorsoft and Spectrum HoloByte worked well together, regularly sharing titles and publishing games in their respective regions.

cues.zh: Spectrum HoloByte 总裁 Phil Adam 当时正在英国物色新游戏，Mackonochie 趁机向他展示了 Tetris。
cues.en: Spectrum HoloByte president Phil Adam was in the UK looking at new titles when Mackonochie showed him Tetris.

cues.zh: 他也上瘾了。
cues.en: He, too, became addicted.

cues.zh: 随后，Robert Stein 与 Maxwell 公司达成了一笔交易。
cues.en: From there, Robert Stein made a deal with the Maxwell Corporation.

cues.zh: Mirrorsoft 以 3000 英镑加版税的价格，拿到了 Tetris 在英国和欧洲的家用电脑及主机版权。
cues.en: Mirrorsoft got the home computer and console rights to Tetris for the UK and Europe for £3000 plus royalties.

cues.zh: Spectrum HoloByte 则以 11000 美元加版税的价格，拿到了美国和日本的版权。
cues.en: Spectrum HoloByte got the rights for the US and Japan for $11,000 plus royalties.

cues.zh: 这对 Stein 来说不算一笔大钱，但他手上还有其他版权可卖，包括街机和掌机版权。
cues.en: It wasn't a huge payday for Stein, but he did have other rights to sell, including the arcade and handheld rights.

cues.zh: 然而，更大的问题在于 Stein 所谓与 Pajitnov 在莫斯科计算中心达成的交易。
cues.en: The bigger problem, however, was Stein's supposed deal with Pajitnov in the computing center in Moscow.

cues.zh: 他只有一封语焉不详的电传消息提到要达成交易，但什么都没签。
cues.en: He had the vague Telex message about making a deal, but nothing was signed.

cues.zh: 严格来说，他是在谈判一款他自己都不拥有的游戏的版权。
cues.en: Technically, he was negotiating the rights to a game he didn't even own.

cues.zh: 与Mirrorsoft和Spectrum HoloByte的合同尚未敲定，时间越来越紧迫。
cues.en: With contracts pending with Mirrorsoft and Spectrum HoloByte, the clock was ticking.

cues.zh: Stein又向莫斯科发了一封电传，提出了他的报价：
cues.en: Stein sent off another Telex message to Moscow with his offer:

cues.zh: 预付1万美元，外加他从俄罗斯方块中所得收益的75%。
cues.en: $10,000 up front, along with 75% on whatever money he made from Tetris.

cues.zh: Pajitnov再次回复了一个含糊但积极的答复。
cues.en: Pajitnov replied once again with a vague, but positive response.

cues.zh: 他们准备达成交易了。
cues.en: They were ready to make a deal.

cues.zh: Stein不断施压。他甚至提出用Commodore电脑来支付部分款项。
cues.en: Stein kept pressing. He even offered partial payment in the form of Commodore computers.

cues.zh: 但正如Pajitnov所预料的，苏联政权介入了谈判。
cues.en: But just as Pajitnov predicted, the Soviet regime intervened in the negotiations.

cues.zh: AcademySoft是俄罗斯科学院内部的一个出版和授权小组，负责处理后续谈判。
cues.en: AcademySoft, an internal publishing and licensing group within the Russian Academy of Sciences, handled further negotiations.

cues.zh: AcademySoft坚持认为，Stein能获得的唯一权利是俄罗斯方块的IBM PC版本。
cues.en: AcademySoft insisted that the only rights available to Stein were for the IBM PC version of Tetris.

cues.zh: Stein同意了；未来版本的Tetris可以稍后再协商。
cues.en: Stein agreed; future versions of Tetris could be negotiated for later.

cues.zh: 此时已是1987年，却仍然没有签署任何合同。
cues.en: It was now 1987, and there were still no signed contracts.

cues.zh: Spectrum HoloByte和Mirrorsoft在假定所有权利都已确保的前提下，各自准备了他们的Tetris版本。
cues.en: Spectrum HoloByte and Mirrorsoft prepared their versions of Tetris under the assumption that all the rights were secured.

cues.zh: Robert Stein越来越沮丧。
cues.en: Robert Stein grew frustrated.

cues.zh: 俄方到底是谁在负责谈判？
cues.en: Who exactly was in charge of the negotiations on the Russian side?

cues.zh: Stein自认为达成了口头协议，但他需要白纸黑字，才能让他与Mirrorsoft和Spectrum HoloByte的交易合法化。
cues.en: Stein had a verbal agreement, or so he thought, but he needed pen to paper in order to make his dealings with Mirrorsoft and Spectrum HoloByte legit.

cues.zh: 于是Stein向俄方施压。
cues.en: So Stein put pressure on the Russians.

cues.zh: 1987年4月，他又向莫斯科发了一封电传，这次宣布Mirrorsoft和Spectrum HoloByte将在各自地区发行IBM PC版Tetris。
cues.en: In April of 1987, he sent another Telex message to Moscow, this time announcing that Mirrorsoft and Spectrum HoloByte would release Tetris for the IBM PC in their respective regions.

cues.zh: 但他的强硬态度没起任何作用。
cues.en: But his forcefulness got him nowhere.

cues.zh: 1987年6月，Stein 敲定了与 Spectrum HoloByte 和 Mirrorsoft 关于 Tetris 的交易。
cues.en: In June of 1987, Stein finalized the deals with Spectrum HoloByte and Mirrorsoft for Tetris.

cues.zh: 但是……他还得让苏联人签字画押。
cues.en: But... he still had to get the Russians to sign on the dotted line.

cues.zh: Robert Stein 向 Spectrum HoloByte 和 Mirrorsoft 保证，他会搞定与苏联人的交易，于是两家公司继续推进 Tetris。
cues.en: Robert Stein assured Spectrum HoloByte and Mirrorsoft that he would secure a deal with the Russians, so the two companies moved forward with Tetris.

cues.zh: 但营销是个大问题。
cues.en: But marketing was a big issue.

cues.zh: Tetris 是款让人上瘾的游戏，但它和市面上任何游戏都不一样。
cues.en: Tetris was an addictive game, but it was unlike any other game on the market.

cues.zh: 没有剧情，也没有英雄；
cues.en: There was no story or hero;

cues.zh: 画面也不够前沿。
cues.en: The graphics weren't cutting-edge.

cues.zh: Spectrum HoloByte 总裁 Phil Adam 指出，Tetris 是第一款在北美商业化的苏联游戏。
cues.en: Phil Adam, president of Spectrum HoloByte, noted that Tetris was the first Russian game to be commercialized in North America.

cues.zh: 为什么不把这变成优势呢？
cues.en: Why not use this to their advantage?

cues.zh: 他提议把 Tetris 包装成一款来自铁幕背后神秘世界的异域游戏来营销。
cues.en: He proposed Tetris be marketed as an exotic game from the mysterious world behind the Iron Curtain.

cues.zh: 这无疑会激发公众对苏联的好奇心。
cues.en: It would surely tap into the public's curiosity about the Soviet Union.

cues.zh: 游戏被完全重新编程，加入了与俄罗斯相关的影射内容。
cues.en: The game was completely reprogrammed to incorporate allusions to Russia.

cues.zh: 开发者加入了圣瓦西里大教堂、列宁体育场和红场五一庆祝活动的图像；
cues.en: The developers added imagery of St. Basil's Cathedral, Lenin Stadium, and May Day celebrations in Red Square;

cues.zh: 他们融入了俄罗斯古典音乐；
cues.en: They incorporated classical Russian music;

cues.zh: 他们甚至加入了对马蒂亚斯·鲁斯特的提及，这位西德飞行员驾驶小型飞机直接飞入红场。
cues.en: They even added a reference to Matthias Rust, a West German pilot who flew a small plane directly into Red Square.

cues.zh: 他被逮捕并被指控犯有流氓罪。
cues.en: He was arrested and charged with hooliganism.

cues.zh: 罗纳德·里根和米哈伊尔·戈尔巴乔夫的模仿者在贸易展上展示了这款游戏。
cues.en: Ronald Reagan and Mikhail Gorbachev impersonators showed off the game at trade shows.

cues.zh: 随着发布日的临近，俄罗斯方块的热度不断增长。
cues.en: The Tetris hype grew as release day approached.

cues.zh: 但就在俄罗斯方块发布前夕，1988年1月，罗伯特·斯坦因收到了来自俄罗斯另一家组织的电传消息。
cues.en: But right before Tetris launched, in January of 1988, Robert Stein received a telex message from another organization in Russia.

cues.zh: 该组织指控Stein非法销售俄罗斯方块，并要求今后的谈判必须通过他们进行。
cues.en: The group accused Stein of selling Tetris illegally, and demanded that further negotiations go through them.

cues.zh: 他们被称为ELORG。
cues.en: They were known as ELORG.

cues.zh: ELORG是Electronicorgtechnica的缩写。
cues.en: ELORG was short for Electronicorgtechnica.

cues.zh: 苏联外贸部成立ELORG的目的是进出口技术，特别是面向其他共产主义国家。
cues.en: The Soviet Ministry of Foreign Trade formed ELORG for the purpose of importing and exporting technology, specifically to other communist nations.

cues.zh: 但在20世纪80年代，在Mikhail Gorbachev的领导下，与西方进行对外贸易的限制放宽了。
cues.en: But in the 1980s, under the leadership of Mikhail Gorbachev, restrictions on foreign trade with the West loosened.

cues.zh: ELORG现在可以自由地在国际上寻求技术授权交易了。
cues.en: ELORG was now free to seek licensing deals for technology internationally.

cues.zh: 这包括计算机软件。
cues.en: This included computer software.

cues.zh: ELORG得知俄罗斯科学院的一些研究人员正在开发计算机程序，包括Pajitnov的人工智能软件。
cues.en: ELORG learned that some of the researchers at the Russian Academy of Sciences were creating computer programs, including Pajitnov's artificial intelligence software.

cues.zh: ELORG与Pajitnov会面，探讨该程序能否在国际上销售。
cues.en: ELORG met with Pajitnov to see if the program could be sold internationally.

cues.zh: 会议期间，Pajitnov随口提到了俄罗斯方块，以及他和AcademySoft在与Robert Stein达成授权协议时遇到的困难。
cues.en: During the meeting, Pajitnov casually mentioned Tetris, and how he and AcademySoft had trouble getting a licensing deal with Robert Stein.

cues.zh: ELORG的代表们大为震惊。
cues.en: Representatives from ELORG were shocked.

cues.zh: Pajitnov和AcademySoft无权谈判国际软件授权协议。
cues.en: Pajitnov and AcademySoft had no authority to negotiate International software licensing deals.

cues.zh: 他们要求立即交出所有相关文件。
cues.en: They demanded all the paperwork be handed over immediately.

cues.zh: 他们了解到的情况令人难以置信。
cues.en: What they learned was incredible.

cues.zh: 俄罗斯科学院的一名研究员竟然在为一款电子游戏谈判国际商业协议！
cues.en: A researcher at the Russian Academy of Sciences was negotiating an international business deal for a video game!

cues.zh: 不仅如此，这款游戏即将在西方销售，而且什么都还没签！
cues.en: Not only that, but it was about to be sold in the West, and nothing had been signed!

cues.zh: 从那时起，ELORG接管了俄罗斯方块的所有谈判。
cues.en: From that point on, ELORG was in charge of all negotiations for Tetris.

cues.zh: 他们请罗伯特·斯坦因来莫斯科当面解释。
cues.en: They asked Robert Stein to come to Moscow to explain himself.

cues.zh: 斯坦因说，他到了之后感觉像在接受审讯。
cues.en: When he arrived, Stein said it felt like an interrogation.

cues.zh: ELORG 的代表们不信任他。
cues.en: Representatives from ELORG didn't trust him.

cues.zh: 他们问：“你为什么未经我们许可就卖俄罗斯方块？”
cues.en: "Why are you selling Tetris without our permission?" they asked.

cues.zh: 斯坦因回答：“我根本不知道你们这个组织的存在！”
cues.en: "I didn't even know your group existed!" Stein replied.

cues.zh: 他坚持立场，辩称现在撤销交易会让苏联难堪，因为这会显得他们在世界经济中不可靠。
cues.en: He held his ground, arguing that pulling the deal now could be an embarrassment to the USSR, as it would make them seem unreliable in the world economy.

cues.zh: 双方你来我往，像一场没完没了的网球赛。
cues.en: The two sides went back and forth in what seemed like a never-ending game of tennis.

cues.zh: ELORG 想要对所有游戏的最终审批权；
cues.en: ELORG wanted final approval over any of the games;

cues.zh: 斯坦因想要所有家用电脑系统的授权，而不只是 IBM PC。
cues.en: Stein wanted the rights to all home computer systems, not just the IBM PC.

cues.zh: 双方继续谈判。
cues.en: The two sides continued to negotiate.

cues.zh: 什么都还没签。
cues.en: Nothing had been signed.

cues.zh: 但在西方，俄罗斯方块继续向前发展。
cues.en: But in the West, Tetris moved forward.

cues.zh: 1988年1月29日，Spectrum HoloByte以34.95美元的价格发行了俄罗斯方块。
cues.en: On January 29 1988, Spectrum HoloByte released Tetris for $34.95.

cues.zh: 它装在一个红色盒子里，上面用粗体黄色俄文字母写着Tetris。
cues.en: It came in a red box with the word Tetris written in Russian in bold yellow characters.

cues.zh: 它在其他游戏中脱颖而出。
cues.en: It stood out from the other games.

cues.zh: 俄罗斯营销角度效果极佳；
cues.en: The Russian marketing angle worked brilliantly;

cues.zh: Spectrum HoloByte第一年就卖出了10万份。
cues.en: Spectrum HoloByte sold 100,000 copies in the first year.

cues.zh: 在英国，Mirrorsoft卖得少一些，但数量仍然可观。
cues.en: In the UK, Mirrorsoft sold fewer, but still a sizable amount.

cues.zh: 不过，他们也从自己的版本中删除了大量俄罗斯意象。
cues.en: Then again, they also removed a lot of the Russian imagery from their version.

cues.zh: 评论界好评如潮。
cues.en: The reviews were glowing.

cues.zh: “俄罗斯方块简单易学，打开盒子五分钟后你就能掌握所有规则。
cues.en: "Tetris is so simple to learn that you`ll know all the rules five minutes after opening the box.

cues.zh: 但玩起来又极其引人入胜，一旦开始，你就会在电脑屏幕前花上许多小时——
cues.en: But it`s so intriguing to play that once you`ve started you`ll be spending many hours in front of the computer screen --

cues.zh: 多到你会开始怀疑，俄罗斯方块是不是邪恶帝国精心策划的阴谋，目的就是降低美国工人的生产力。”
cues.en: so many that you`ll begin to wonder if Tetris isn`t really part of a diabolical plot hatched in the Evil Empire to lower worker productivity in the United States."

cues.zh: Dennis Lynch，芝加哥论坛报。
cues.en: Dennis Lynch, Chicago Tribune.

cues.zh: 就电脑游戏而言，它简单又让人上瘾。
cues.en: "As computer games go, it is simple and addictive.

cues.zh: 批评者说它缺少枪战、爆炸和混乱场面，而这些正是美国娱乐软件年轻行家们喜欢的，不过话说回来，苏联软件显然走的是软路线。
cues.en: Critics say it lacks the guns and explosions and mayhem that appeal to young connoisseurs of American entertainment software, but then, Soviet software is apparently softline."

cues.zh: Peter Lewis，纽约时报。
cues.en: Peter Lewis, the New York Times.

cues.zh: 俄罗斯方块热潮席卷西方，人们在家里和工作中都在玩。
cues.en: Tetris fever enveloped the West and was being played at home and at work.

cues.zh: Spectrum HoloByte甚至给游戏加了个老板键：
cues.en: Spectrum HoloByte even added a boss key to the game:

cues.zh: 按下escape键会迅速调出一个空白的命令提示符。
cues.en: Pressing the escape button would quickly bring up a blank command prompt.

cues.zh: 对Spectrum HoloByte和Mirrorsoft来说，这是一次巨大的成功。
cues.en: To Spectrum HoloByte and Mirrorsoft, it was a resounding success.

cues.zh: 但Robert Stein很紧张；
cues.en: But Robert Stein was nervous;

cues.zh: 他与俄罗斯人的交易仍悬而未决。
cues.en: His deal with the Russians was still in limbo.

cues.zh: Spectrum HoloByte和Mirrorsoft开始将游戏移植到其他电脑平台。
cues.en: Spectrum HoloByte and Mirrorsoft began porting the game to other computer platforms.

cues.zh: 但最终，在1988年5月，也就是俄罗斯方块上市四个月后，ELORG和Robert Stein达成了协议。
cues.en: But finally, in May of 1988, four months after Tetris hit the market, ELORG and Robert Stein made a deal.

cues.zh: Andromeda Software获得了俄罗斯方块在家用电脑系统上的版权。
cues.en: Andromeda Software got the rights to Tetris for home computer systems.

cues.zh: 他们还获得了将俄罗斯方块移植到所谓的“……不同类型的电脑……”上的权利。
cues.en: They also got the rights to port Tetris to quote, "...different types of computers..."

cues.zh: 对Stein来说，这也意味着家用游戏主机。
cues.en: To Stein, this meant home consoles as well.

cues.zh: ELORG预先收到了一笔未披露金额的款项，以及每售出一份游戏的版税。
cues.en: ELORG received an undisclosed amount up front, as well as royalties on every game sold.

cues.zh: Stein松了一口气。
cues.en: Stein breathed a sigh of relief.

cues.zh: 他立刻打电话给Mirrorsoft的Jim Mackonochie，确认交易已正式完成。
cues.en: He quickly phoned Jim Mackonochie at Mirrorsoft, confirming the deal was officially done.

cues.zh: 当Mackonochie询问街机和掌机版权时，Stein向他保证那笔交易也即将达成。
cues.en: When Mackonochie asked about the arcade and handheld rights, Stein assured him that deal was imminent as well.

cues.zh: 由此，他们编织了一张错综复杂的再许可网络，最终演变成一场关于谁能在俄罗斯方块上做什么的激烈争夺战。
cues.en: From there, they wove a tangled web of sublicenses that would ultimately turn into a ferocious battle over who could do what with Tetris.

cues.zh: 1988年1月，Spectrum HoloByte在拉斯维加斯冬季消费电子展上展示了他们的新产品。
cues.en: In January of 1988, Spectrum HoloByte showed off their new product at the winter Consumer Electronics Show in Las Vegas.

cues.zh: Spectrum HoloByte总裁Phil Adam自豪地站在展厅里，向排着长队的参会者展示《俄罗斯方块》。
cues.en: Spectrum HoloByte president Phil Adam stood proudly on the showroom floor displaying Tetris to a long line of attendees.

cues.zh: 队伍中站着Henk Rogers，他是日本游戏发行商Bullet-Proof Software的老板。
cues.en: Standing in that line was Henk Rogers, owner of Japanese game publisher Bullet-Proof Software.

cues.zh: Rogers出生于荷兰，但在美国长大。
cues.en: Rogers was born in the Netherlands, but grew up in the United States.

cues.zh: 在夏威夷大学读书时，他爱上了一位日本女性，并随她搬回了日本。
cues.en: While in college at the University of Hawaii, he fell in love with a Japanese woman, and moved back to Japan with her.

cues.zh: 在那里，他进入了游戏开发领域，并创立了Bullet-Proof Software。
cues.en: From there, he got into game development, and formed Bullet-Proof Software.

cues.zh: 受游戏《龙与地下城》的启发，Henk Rogers推出了《黑玛瑙》，这是一款雄心勃勃的回合制RPG，日本此前从未见过这样的作品。
cues.en: Inspired by the game Dungeons & Dragons, Henk Rogers released The Black Onyx, an ambitious turn-based RPG the likes of which Japan had never seen before.

cues.zh: 到1984年底，它成了日本最畅销的电脑游戏。
cues.en: By the end of 1984, it was the best-selling computer game in Japan.

cues.zh: 1985年，他迷上了任天堂红白机，决心为这个平台做一款游戏。
cues.en: In 1985, he was enamored with the Nintendo Famicom, and determined to make a game for the system.

cues.zh: 他在杂志上读到任天堂社长山内溥是围棋爱好者，于是安排了一次会面。
cues.en: After reading in a magazine that Nintendo president Hiroshi Yamauchi was a fan of the board game Go, he set up a meeting.

cues.zh: Rogers 提出他可以为红白机做围棋游戏。
cues.en: Rogers pitched that he could make Go for the Famicom.

cues.zh: 山内给了他3000万日元的预付款，约合30万美元，用来开发这款游戏。
cues.en: Yamauchi gave him an advance of ¥30 million, or approximately $300,000 to make the game.

cues.zh: 几分钟内，Rogers 就和任天堂达成了协议，拿到了现金，成为任天堂的正式授权开发商。
cues.en: Within minutes, Rogers had a deal with Nintendo, cash, and became an official Nintendo licensee.

cues.zh: 到1988年，Rogers 越来越多地涉足发行业务。
cues.en: By 1988, Rogers was getting more into publishing.

cues.zh: 他常去参加行业展会，寻找下一款能带回日本的大作。
cues.en: He frequented trade shows looking for the next big game to bring back to Japan.

cues.zh: 于是他就站在那里，排队等着玩一款来自俄罗斯、样子古怪的新游戏：
cues.en: So there he stood, waiting in line to play an odd-looking new game from Russia:

cues.zh: 俄罗斯方块。
cues.en: Tetris.

cues.zh: 他不太确定该怎么看待它。
cues.en: He wasn't quite sure what to make of it.

cues.zh: “俄罗斯方块可能是展会上最安静的游戏。
cues.en: "Tetris was probably the quietest game at the show.

cues.zh: 即便在当时，产品在画面上已经很刺激了，但这款游戏完全是另一回事。
cues.en: Even then, products were graphically exciting, but this game was a totally different thing.

cues.zh: 我想玩它，因为它触动了我内心的某根弦。
cues.en: I wanted to play it because it struck some basic chord.

cues.zh: 我玩得停不下来。”
cues.en: I couldn't stop playing."

cues.zh: 排队玩了五遍以上之后，Rogers 确信：俄罗斯方块就是他一直在找的游戏。
cues.en: After going through the line more than five times to play, Rogers was convinced: Tetris was the game he was looking for.

cues.zh: 它很简单，看起来容易编程，而且几乎不需要翻译。
cues.en: It was simple, seemed easy to program, and would require little translation.

cues.zh: Rogers 得知，Spectrum HoloByte 的 CEO Gilman Louie 要去日本物色游戏。
cues.en: Rogers learned that Gilman Louie, CEO of Spectrum HoloByte, was going to Japan to shop the game.

cues.zh: Gilman Louie 的第一站是 ASCII 公司，日本最大的发行商之一。
cues.en: Gilman Louie's first stop was the ASCII Corporation, one of the largest publishers in Japan.

cues.zh: 他们拒绝了俄罗斯方块，说它太复古了。
cues.en: They declined Tetris, saying it was too Retro.

cues.zh: 他们的损失成了 Rogers 的收获。
cues.en: Their loss was Rogers' gain.

cues.zh: Gilman Louie和Henk Rogers签署了一份意向书，让Bullet-Proof Software在日本发行Tetris，覆盖几乎所有能想到的平台。
cues.en: Gilman Louie and Henk Rogers signed a letter of intent for Bullet-Proof Software to publish Tetris in Japan for just about every platform Imaginable.

cues.zh: Rogers的报价很标准：一笔现金预付款，外加每售出一份的版税。
cues.en: Rogers' offer was standard: a cash advance as well as royalties on every copy sold.

cues.zh: Spectrum HoloByte没有进军日本市场的计划，而Rogers似乎完全有能力把Tetris带到这个国家。
cues.en: Spectrum HoloByte had no plans for getting into the Japanese market, and Rogers seemed more than capable of delivering Tetris to the country.

cues.zh: 当Gilman Louie打电话给Mirrorsoft的Jim Mackonochie告知这个消息时，他得到了一个意外。
cues.en: When Gilman Louie phoned Jim Mackonochie at Mirrorsoft to tell him the news, he received a surprise.

cues.zh: Rogers拿不到日本的主机和街机版权，因为这些已经卖出去了。
cues.en: Rogers couldn't have the console and arcade rights for Japan, because those were already sold.

cues.zh: 买家是Atari Games，他们计划通过子公司Tengen来发行这些游戏。
cues.en: The buyer was Atari Games, which planned to publish the games under their subsidiary, Tengen.

cues.zh: 和其他人一样，Atari Games的工程师们也在玩PC版Tetris，而且都上瘾了。
cues.en: Like everyone else, engineers at Atari Games were playing the PC version of Tetris, and were addicted.

cues.zh: 这事在办公室里成了大家茶余饭后的谈资，也促使Atari Games出手拿下版权。
cues.en: It became common water-cooler talk at the office, which motivated Atari Games to grab the rights.

cues.zh: 更糟的是，Atari Games几乎是白菜价就拿到了。
cues.en: To make matters worse for Rogers, Atari Games got it for a steal.

cues.zh: 作为交换日本和北美的主机与街机版权，Atari Games把《Blasteroids》的PC版权给了Mirrorsoft——那不过是街机游戏《Asteroids》的浅层翻新。
cues.en: In exchange for console and arcade rights in Japan and North America, Atari Games gave Mirrorsoft the PC rights to Blasteroids, a shallow update of the arcade game Asteroids.

cues.zh: 没有版税，也没有现金对价。
cues.en: No royalties or cash to consider.

cues.zh: Gilman Louie气坏了，但他无能为力。
cues.en: Gilman Louie was furious, but there was nothing he could do.

cues.zh: Mirrorsoft凭借与Maxwell Corporation的直接关系，握有更大的权力。
cues.en: Mirrorsoft had more power thanks to their direct connection to the Maxwell Corporation.

cues.zh: Louie打电话给Henk Rogers告知了这个消息。
cues.en: Louie phoned Henk Rogers to give him the news.

cues.zh: Rogers可以拿到PC版权，但如果他想要主机和街机版权，就得去联系Atari Games。
cues.en: Rogers could have the PC rights, but if he wanted the console and arcade rights, he would have to contact Atari Games.

cues.zh: Rogers联系他们询问版权事宜，Atari Games拒绝了。
cues.en: When Rogers contacted them and inquired about the rights, Atari Games declined.

cues.zh: Rogers 没有气馁，他飞到加州，在 Atari Games 的停车场里安营扎寨。
cues.en: Undeterred, Rogers flew to California and camped out in the Atari Games parking lot.

cues.zh: 他等待机会和他们的总裁 Hideyuki Nakajima 谈谈。
cues.en: He waited for an opportunity to talk to their president, Hideyuki Nakajima.

cues.zh: 趁 Nakajima 当天离开时，Rogers 冲上前去，推销了一番。
cues.en: As Nakajima was leaving for the day, Rogers swooped in and made his sales pitch.

cues.zh: 最终，Nakajima 同意会面。
cues.en: Eventually, Nakajima agreed to a meeting.

cues.zh: 在一顿寿司晚餐上，两位商人敲定了细节。
cues.en: Over a sushi dinner, the two businessmen hashed out the details.

cues.zh: Nakajima 无法出售街机版权；他已经把它们卖给了 Sega。
cues.en: Nakajima couldn't sell the arcade rights; he had already sold them to Sega.

cues.zh: 但他愿意出售日本的游戏机版权。
cues.en: But he was willing to sell the console rights in Japan.

cues.zh: Nakajima 并不太在意拥有日本的游戏机版权，因为他正专注于北美市场。
cues.en: Nakajima didn't care too much about having the console rights in Japan, because he was focusing on the North American market.

cues.zh: 价格很高：Rogers 不得不掏出 30 万美元购买游戏机版权。
cues.en: The price tag was steep: Rogers had to cough up $300,000 for the console rights.

cues.zh: 但他确信这款游戏会大获成功。
cues.en: But he was confident the game was a hit.

cues.zh: 然而，最初在日本的销量很低。
cues.en: However, initial sales in Japan were low.

cues.zh: Bullet-Proof Software 只收到了 4 万份订单。
cues.en: Bullet-Proof Software only received 40,000 orders.

cues.zh: Rogers 联系了任天堂总裁山内溥，希望他能帮忙推动这款游戏。
cues.en: Rogers contacted Nintendo president Hiroshi Yamauchi in hopes that he could help push the game.

cues.zh: 山内溥很好奇，于是把 Tetris 交给了手下的一位设计师宫本茂。
cues.en: Yamauchi was curious, so he passed Tetris down to one of his designers, Shigeru Miyamoto.

cues.zh: 几天后，山口问宫本茂 Tetris 是不是一款好游戏。
cues.en: Several days later, Yamaguchi asked Miyamoto if Tetris was a good game.

cues.zh: “是的，”宫本茂回答。
cues.en: "Yes," replied Miyamoto.

cues.zh: 当山口问为什么时，宫本茂回答：
cues.en: When Yamaguchi asked why, Miyamoto responded:

cues.zh: “因为你的秘书和会计都在玩它。”
cues.en: "Because your secretaries and accountants are playing it."

cues.zh: 由此，山内溥明白了 Tetris 的普适吸引力，并同意帮助推动 Tetris 的销售。
cues.en: With that, Yamauchi understood Tetris' universal appeal, and he agreed to help push sales of Tetris.

cues.zh: 订单从 4 万份增加到了超过 20 万份。
cues.en: Orders increased from 40,000 to over 200,000.

cues.zh: 1988 年 12 月 22 日，Bullet-Proof Software 为 Nintendo Famicom 发行了 Tetris，它成为了他们有史以来最畅销的游戏，卖出了 200 万份。
cues.en: On December 22nd, 1988, Bullet-Proof Software released Tetris for the Nintendo Famicom, where it became their best selling game of all time, selling 2 million copies.

cues.zh: 但这又给本就复杂的授权与再授权体系添了新的分支。
cues.en: But it added yet another branch to a complicated tree of licensing and sub--licensing.

cues.zh: 一切都系于一份合同：Robert Stein 与 ELORG 的俄罗斯人达成的协议……而这份协议正岌岌可危。
cues.en: Everything hinged on one contract: Robert Stein's deal with the Russians at ELORG... and that deal was in jeopardy.

cues.zh: 1988 年，任天堂正处于电子游戏世界的顶峰。
cues.en: In 1988, Nintendo was on top of the video game world.

cues.zh: 那一年，他们有望卖出七百万台 Nintendo Entertainment System。
cues.en: They were on pace to sell seven million Nintendo Entertainment Systems that year.

cues.zh: 业内专家预测，任天堂游戏的市场比所有家用电脑软件加起来还要大。
cues.en: Industry experts predicted the market for Nintendo games was larger than all home computer software.

cues.zh: 而且他们还没停下脚步。
cues.en: And they weren't done yet.

cues.zh: 日本任天堂正在幕后筹备一款新主机：掌机 Game Boy。
cues.en: Waiting in the wings at Nintendo of Japan was a new system: the handheld Game Boy.

cues.zh: 在北美，新主机捆绑一款游戏发售是惯例，但选哪一款呢？
cues.en: In North America, it was standard to package new Nintendo consoles with a game, but which one?

cues.zh: 1988 年 12 月，Henk Rogers 在华盛顿州雷德蒙德的任天堂美国总部，与总裁 Minoru Arakawa 会面。
cues.en: In December of 1988, Henk Rogers was meeting with Nintendo of America president Minoru Arakawa at their headquarters in Redmond, Washington.

cues.zh: Rogers听说他们的情况后，建议用Tetris。
cues.en: When Rogers heard about their situation, he suggested Tetris.

cues.zh: “如果搭上Mario，Game Boy就只是给小男孩玩的。
cues.en: "If you include Mario, the Game Boy will be for little boys.

cues.zh: 但如果搭上Tetris，Game Boy就是给所有人的，”他说。
cues.en: But if you include Tetris, the Game Boy will be for everybody," he said.

cues.zh: Arakawa很感兴趣。
cues.en: Arakawa was intrigued.

cues.zh: 他听说了Tetris在日本Famicom上的成功。
cues.en: He heard about the success of Tetris for the Famicom in Japan.

cues.zh: Tengen正准备在北美为Nintendo Entertainment System发行Tetris，但掌机版权仍悬而未决。
cues.en: Tengen was preparing to release Tetris for the Nintendo Entertainment System in North America, but the handheld rights were still up for grabs.

cues.zh: Rogers非常乐意帮忙。
cues.en: Rogers was more than happy to help.

cues.zh: 他知道这笔交易能赚几百万，尤其是如果Tetris成为捆绑游戏的话。
cues.en: He knew he could make millions in this deal, especially if Tetris was a pack-in title.

cues.zh: 在日本拿下Tetris版权的经历之后，他知道该找的人是Robert Stein。
cues.en: After his experience getting the Tetris rights in Japan, he knew that Robert Stein was the man to talk to.

cues.zh: Rogers打电话给Stein，询问Tetris的掌机版权。
cues.en: Rogers called Stein and inquired about the handheld rights to Tetris.

cues.zh: 他预付了25,000美元。
cues.en: He offered $25,000 in advance.

cues.zh: Stein当时还没拿到掌机和街机版权，同时也在应付Mirrorsoft打来的电话，对方想要掌机版权。
cues.en: Stein, who still didn't have the handheld or arcade rights, was also fielding calls for Mirrorsoft, asking for the handheld rights.

cues.zh: 他的回应含糊其辞。
cues.en: He was wishy-washy in his response.

cues.zh: 他得先跟俄罗斯人确认，再回复Rogers。
cues.en: He would have to check with the Russians and get back to Rogers.

cues.zh: 但Stein即将撞上又一个路障。
cues.en: But Stein was about to hit another roadblock.

cues.zh: 在错综复杂的授权网络中，ELORG一直没收到钱。
cues.en: Somewhere in the tangled web of licensing, ELORG wasn't getting paid.

cues.zh: 他们派新任总监Nikoli Belikov去收拾这个烂摊子。
cues.en: They tasked their new director, Nikoli Belikov, with sorting out the mess.

cues.zh: Belikov身材高大，以手段狠辣著称。
cues.en: Belikov was a large man with a reputation for being cutthroat.

cues.zh: Pajitnov形容他是“一个出色的演员”。
cues.en: Pajitnov described him as, "an excellent actor."

cues.zh: 他是个难缠的谈判对手。
cues.en: He was a worthy negotiator.

cues.zh: Belikov读了Stein与ELORG于1988年5月签署的合同。
cues.en: Belikov read Stein and ELORG's contract, which was signed in May of 1988.

cues.zh: 合同承诺三个月内付款。
cues.en: It promised payment within three months.

cues.zh: 如今这笔款项已逾期三个月。
cues.en: The payment was now three months overdue.

cues.zh: Stein 陷入了困境。
cues.en: Stein was stuck.

cues.zh: Mirrorsoft 和 Henk Rogers 都想要掌机版权；
cues.en: He had Mirrorsoft and Henk Rogers wanting handheld rights;

cues.zh: 未经授权的街机版俄罗斯方块已经在售卖了。
cues.en: Unlicensed arcade versions of Tetris were already being sold.

cues.zh: 他觉得解决问题的最好办法是飞往莫斯科，与 Belikov 会面。
cues.en: He figured his best chance to sort everything out was to fly to Moscow and meet with Belikov.

cues.zh: 与此同时，Henk Rogers 觉得自己被忽视了。
cues.en: Meanwhile, Henk Rogers felt ignored.

cues.zh: 他对 Robert Stein 起了疑心。
cues.en: He grew suspicious of Robert Stein.

cues.zh: 不仅如此，他还得知 Spectrum HoloByte 的 Gilman Louie 正试图把俄罗斯方块的掌机版权卖给任天堂。
cues.en: Not only that, but he got word that Gilman Louie of Spectrum HoloByte was trying to sell the handheld rights for Tetris to Nintendo.

cues.zh: 当 Minoru Arakawa 向 Rogers 问起此事时，Rogers 态度坚决。
cues.en: When Minoru Arakawa asked Rogers about it, Rogers was adamant.

cues.zh: “我知道 Gilman 没有那些版权。
cues.en: "I know Gilman doesn't have those rights.

cues.zh: 给我一个机会，让我把那笔交易敲定。”
cues.en: Give me a chance to finalize that deal."

cues.zh: Rogers 认定，自己直接和俄罗斯人打交道会更省事，于是动身前往莫斯科。
cues.en: Rogers decided that it would be easier if he just dealt with the Russians himself, and headed off to Moscow.

cues.zh: 在英国，Mirrorsoft 得知了任天堂对掌机版权感兴趣的消息。
cues.en: In the UK, Mirrorsoft caught wind of Nintendo's interest in handheld rights.

cues.zh: 母公司Maxwell Corporation派了老板Robert Maxwell的儿子Kevin Maxwell去莫斯科。
cues.en: Parent company Maxwell Corporation sent Kevin Maxwell, the son of owner Robert Maxwell, to Moscow.

cues.zh: Maxwell Corporation和俄罗斯外交官有关系，拿下掌机和街机版权会更有优势。
cues.en: Maxwell Corporation had connections with Russian diplomats, and would have much more power securing the handheld and arcade rights.

cues.zh: 1989年2月，Stein、Rogers和Maxwell三个人都飞到了莫斯科，想分Tetris这杯羹。
cues.en: In February of 1989, all three men: Stein, Rogers, and Maxwell, flew to Moscow to get their piece of the Tetris pie.

cues.zh: Tetris争夺战即将打响。
cues.en: The battle for Tetris was about to begin.

cues.zh: Henk Rogers到了莫斯科，完全不知道该去哪儿。
cues.en: Henk Rogers arrived in Moscow without any clue where to go.

cues.zh: 他知道Stein正在和ELORG谈判，但就是找不到他们的下落。
cues.en: He knew Stein was negotiating with ELORG, but he had trouble finding their whereabouts.

cues.zh: 一开始他想靠和当地人下围棋交朋友，但毫无进展。
cues.en: At first, he tried to make friends by playing Go with some locals, but that got him nowhere.

cues.zh: 于是Rogers雇了个翻译帮他找ELORG。
cues.en: So Rogers hired an interpreter to help him find ELORG.

cues.zh: 在莫斯科转了一整天，他们终于找到了地址。
cues.en: After a day of riding around Moscow, they finally got the location.

cues.zh: Henk Rogers 走进 ELORG，要求找人谈谈俄罗斯方块的版权。
cues.en: Henk Rogers walked into ELORG and asked to speak to someone about the rights to Tetris.

cues.zh: 他在大厅等候时，能感觉到那种紧张气氛。
cues.en: As he waited in the lobby, he could feel the tension.

cues.zh: “你不会未经邀请就走进那种地方，”他说。
cues.en: "You don't walk into a place like that uninvited," he said.

cues.zh: 当 Belikov 得知一个来自日本的外国人前来洽谈俄罗斯方块时，他很惊讶。
cues.en: When Belikov was told a foreigner from Japan had come to discuss Tetris, he was surprised.

cues.zh: 未经适当许可与外国人会面是违反政府规定的，但 Belikov 很好奇，决定见见他。
cues.en: It was against government protocol to meet with foreigners without proper clearance, but Belikov was curious and decided to meet him.

cues.zh: 至少，有第三个竞标者参与俄罗斯方块的谈判，对他的谈判会有帮助。
cues.en: If nothing else, having a third bidder for Tetris would help in his negotiations.

cues.zh: Belikov 在大厅见到了 Rogers。
cues.en: Belikov met Rogers in the lobby.

cues.zh: “你是谁？”他问道。
cues.en: "Who are you?" he asked.

cues.zh: Rogers 拿出一份 Famicom 上的俄罗斯方块，递给 Belikov。
cues.en: Rogers took out a copy of Tetris on the Famicom and handed it to Belikov.

cues.zh: “我们现在是世界上最大的俄罗斯方块发行商，”他夸口道。
cues.en: "We are the biggest publisher of Tetris in the world right now," he boasted.

cues.zh: Belikov看着这款游戏，一脸困惑。
cues.en: Belikov looked at the game, confused.

cues.zh: 据他所知，没人拥有俄罗斯方块的游戏机版权。
cues.en: As far as he knew, no one had the console rights to Tetris.

cues.zh: “ELORG根本没把电子游戏机版权给过任何人！”Belikov厉声说道。
cues.en: "ELORG hasn't given video game console rights to anyone!" Belikov barked.

cues.zh: Rogers据理力争，解释了让他获得授权的那一连串许可与再许可：
cues.en: Rogers made his case, explaining the chain of licensing and sub-licensing that gave him the rights:

cues.zh: ELORG授权给Andromeda，再到Mirrorsoft，再到Tengen，再到Bullet-Proof Software。
cues.en: ELORG, to Andromeda, to Mirrorsoft, to Tengen, to Bullet-Proof Software.

cues.zh: Belikov一头雾水。
cues.en: Belikov was confused.

cues.zh: 他压根没听说过Tengen。
cues.en: He had never even heard of Tengen.

cues.zh: “版权只转让给了Andromeda Software，而且仅限于在个人电脑上使用俄罗斯方块！
cues.en: "The only rights were transferred to Andromeda Software, and only for using Tetris on personal computers!

cues.zh: 你这是在非法售卖不属于你的东西！”他说。
cues.en: You are illegally selling something that doesn't belong to you!" he said.

cues.zh: Rogers来莫斯科本是为了拿下掌机版权，可现在他面临失去一切的危险。
cues.en: Rogers had come to Moscow to secure the handheld rights, but now he was in danger of losing everything.

cues.zh: “要么我带着俄罗斯方块的版权走出这里，要么我就得进古拉格了，”他心想。
cues.en: 'Either I'm going to come out of here with the rights to Tetris, or I'm going to be in some gulag,' he thought.

cues.zh: 经过一番讨论，Rogers和Belikov约定第二天会面。
cues.en: After some discussion, Rogers and Belikov set up a meeting for the next day.

cues.zh: 第二天，Henk Rogers来到ELORG，被领进一间摆着巨大桌子的宽敞房间。
cues.en: The next day, Henk Rogers arrived at ELORG and was ushered into a large room with a massive table.

cues.zh: 桌子一端坐着ELORG的谈判代表Nikoli Belikov、俄罗斯方块创造者Alexey Pajitnov，以及几位ELORG团队成员。
cues.en: On one end of the table was ELORG's negotiator, Nikoli Belikov, Tetris creator Alexey Pajitnov, and several members of the ELORG team.

cues.zh: Henk Rogers独自坐在另一端。
cues.en: Henk Rogers sat alone on the other side.

cues.zh: 通常，他的推销会强调自己与任天堂的紧密关系，以及任天堂如何占据视频游戏市场的大部分份额。
cues.en: Usually, his sales pitches touched on his close connection with Nintendo, and how they had a majority of the video game market share.

cues.zh: 但俄罗斯人对任天堂和视频游戏市场一无所知。
cues.en: But the Russians didn't know anything about Nintendo, or the video game market.

cues.zh: 于是他转变策略，给他们上了一堂视频游戏行业的速成课。
cues.en: So he shifted gears, and gave them a crash course on the video game business.

cues.zh: ELORG向Rogers展示了他们与Andromeda Software的Robert Stein签订的原始合同。
cues.en: ELORG showed Rogers their original contract with Robert Stein of Andromeda Software.

cues.zh: Rogers 扫描了它，找到了引发所有问题的那一行。
cues.en: Rogers scanned it, and found the line that was causing all the trouble.

cues.zh: Andromeda Software 与 ELORG 之间的合同规定，Stein 有权将 Tetris 移植到所谓的“……不同类型的计算机……”上。
cues.en: The contract between Andromeda Software and ELORG stated that Stein had the rights to port Tetris to quote, "...different types of computers..."

cues.zh: 对俄罗斯人来说，这意思很明确：计算机系统。
cues.en: To the Russians, this meant exactly that: computer systems.

cues.zh: 对 Stein 来说，计算机系统和游戏主机之间并不存在区别。
cues.en: To Stein, the distinction between computer system and console didn't exist.

cues.zh: 除此之外，ELORG 从 Tetris 上只赚到一点小钱；百分之一的百分之一。
cues.en: On top of that, ELORG was making pennies on Tetris; a percent of a percent.

cues.zh: 这是一份糟糕透顶的合同。
cues.en: It was a horrible contract.

cues.zh: Rogers 向 ELORG 陈述了自己的理由，详细解释了他对掌机版权的报价。
cues.en: Rogers made his case to ELORG, explaining his offer for handheld rights in detail.

cues.zh: 他提出按每份售出的卡带支付固定金额。
cues.en: He offered a fixed amount for each cartridge sold.

cues.zh: 在和 Robert Stein 打交道之后，这真是让人耳目一新的转变。
cues.en: It was a nice change of pace after dealing with Robert Stein.

cues.zh: 尤其是 Pajitnov，对此印象深刻。
cues.en: Pajitnov, in particular, was impressed.

cues.zh: Rogers 懂商业运作，但作为前开发者，两人惺惺相惜。
cues.en: Rogers understood the business end of things, but as a former developer, the two were kindred spirits.

cues.zh: Rogers 推销之后，Belikov 想继续推进，并要求就 Tetris 掌机版权给出正式报价。
cues.en: After Rogers' pitch, Belikov wanted to move forward and asked for a formal offer for handheld rights to Tetris.

cues.zh: “把一切都写下来，”他说。
cues.en: "Write everything down," he said.

cues.zh: Belikov 随后问 Rogers 什么时候会回莫斯科。
cues.en: Belikov then asked Rogers when he would be back in Moscow.

cues.zh: “要么带着交易走，要么不带交易走。我不会再回来了，”Rogers 回答。
cues.en: "Either I leave with the deal or without the deal. I'm not coming back," Rogers replied.

cues.zh: 会议结束后，Henk Rogers 和 Alexey Pajitnov 继续交谈。
cues.en: After the meeting, Henk Rogers and Alexey Pajitnov continued talking.

cues.zh: “不知怎的，我们几乎立刻就喜欢上了对方。
cues.en: "Somehow we liked each other almost immediately.

cues.zh: 他正是我在俄罗斯寻找的朋友，”Rogers 说。
cues.en: He was the friend I was looking for in Russia," said Rogers.

cues.zh: 那天晚上，Pajitnov 带 Rogers 逛了莫斯科。
cues.en: That night, Pajitnov showed Rogers around Moscow.

cues.zh: 他们探索了这座城市，喝了伏特加，还讨论了 Tetris 续作的想法。
cues.en: They explored the city, drank vodka;, and discussed ideas for a sequel to Tetris.

cues.zh: 对 Pajitnov 来说，能随意聊聊自己的创作令人耳目一新。
cues.en: For Pajitnov, it was refreshing to have a casual conversation about his creation.

cues.zh: “他什么都没给我，也什么都没要，”他说。
cues.en: "He offered me nothing and asked for nothing," he said.

cues.zh: 两人结下的友谊将对俄罗斯方块的未来产生重大影响。
cues.en: The two formed a friendship that would have a major impact on the future of Tetris.

cues.zh: 第二天，Rogers 带着一份一页纸的报价回到 ELORG，求购俄罗斯方块的手持设备版权。
cues.en: The next day, Rogers returned to ELORG with a one-page offer for the handheld rights to Tetris.

cues.zh: Rogers 知道 Stein 会来，于是施压，让这份报价一周内到期。
cues.en: Rogers knew Stein would be coming, so he added pressure by having the offer expire in one week.

cues.zh: 在速成电子游戏生意经之后，Nikoli Belikov 为即将与 Robert Stein 和 Kevin Maxwell 的会面做准备。
cues.en: After his crash course on the video game business, Nikoli Belikov prepared for his upcoming meetings with Robert Stein and Kevin Maxwell.

cues.zh: Belikov 认为 Stein 在滥用他对俄罗斯方块的权利。
cues.en: Belikov thought Stein was abusing his rights to Tetris.

cues.zh: Stein 拿走了所有好处，而俄罗斯人几乎一无所获。
cues.en: Stein reaped all the rewards, while the Russians got next to nothing.

cues.zh: 同样明显的是，俄罗斯方块创作者 Alexey Pajitnov 更青睐 Rogers 而非 Stein。
cues.en: It was also apparent that Tetris creator Alexey Pajitnov preferred Rogers over Stein.

cues.zh: 是时候让共产党人来玩资本主义这场游戏了。
cues.en: it was time for the Communists to play the game of capitalism.

cues.zh: Robert Stein 走进 ELORG 办公室，心里只有一个目标：拿下俄罗斯方块的手持设备和街机版权。
cues.en: Robert Stein entered the ELORG offices with one goal in mind: to secure the handheld and arcade rights to Tetris.

cues.zh: 考虑到Tengen和Sega已经在销售机器，街机版权尤为重要。
cues.en: The arcade rights were especially important, considering Tengen and Sega were already selling machines.

cues.zh: 但Nikoli Belikov另有打算。
cues.en: But Nikoli Belikov had other plans.

cues.zh: Belikov向Stein出示了他们最初的合同。
cues.en: Belikov presented Stein with their original contract.

cues.zh: “Stein先生：老实告诉我，这份文件叫什么？”他问道。
cues.en: "Mr. Stein: tell me honestly, what is this document called?" he asked.

cues.zh: “一份协议，”Stein回答。
cues.en: "An agreement," replied Stein.

cues.zh: “这不是协议！”Belikov厉声说道。
cues.en: "It's not an agreement!" snapped Belikov.

cues.zh: “这是一堆不负责任的措辞，根据这些措辞，权利被转让给一方，而另一方却得不到补偿！”
cues.en: "It's a set of some irresponsible phrases or other, under which rights are transferred to one party without compensation for the other!"

cues.zh: Belikov向Stein出示了原合同的修正案。
cues.en: Belikov presented Stein with an amendment to the original contract.

cues.zh: ELORG想要他们的钱，所以修正案详细规定了逾期付款的罚则。
cues.en: ELORG wanted their money, so the amendment detailed penalties for late payment.

cues.zh: Belikov拒绝谈判，直到Stein签字。
cues.en: Belikov refused to negotiate until Stein signed it.

cues.zh: Stein同意仔细阅读修正案，几天后再回来。
cues.en: Stein agreed to read over the amendment, and return in a few days.

cues.zh: 那场会面不算友好，但Stein相信，等一切平息下来，他就能拿下掌机和街机版权。
cues.en: It wasn't the friendliest meeting, but Stein was confident that once all of this was smoothed over, he would secure the handheld and arcade rights.

cues.zh: Belikov的下一次会面对象是Kevin Maxwell，Maxwell Corporation老板Robert Maxwell的儿子。
cues.en: Belikov's next meeting was with Kevin Maxwell, the son of Maxwell Corporation owner Robert Maxwell.

cues.zh: Robert Maxwell与俄罗斯官僚有联系，包括总书记Mikhail Gorbachev。
cues.en: Robert Maxwell had connections to Russian bureaucrats, including general secretary Mikhail Gorbachev.

cues.zh: Mirrorsoft相信Kevin Maxwell会推动事情朝有利于他们的方向发展，从而拿下掌机版权。
cues.en: Mirrorsoft was confident that Kevin Maxwell would get the ball rolling in their favor to secure the handheld rights.

cues.zh: Belikov开场就把Famicom俄罗斯方块包装盒从桌面推了过去。
cues.en: Belikov began the meeting by sliding the Famicom Tetris box across the table.

cues.zh: “这是什么？”他装傻道。
cues.en: "What is this?" he bluffed.

cues.zh: Maxwell完全不知道。他猜那是俄罗斯方块的盗版。
cues.en: Maxwell had no idea. He guessed It was a pirated copy of Tetris.

cues.zh: “这更说明Mirrorsoft和ELORG该达成协议，把这些假货清掉，”他说。
cues.en: "Only more reason for Mirrorsoft and ELORG to make a deal and get rid of these fakes," he said.

cues.zh: Maxwell对局势的无知，正是他的败因。
cues.en: Maxwell's ignorance of the situation was his downfall.

cues.zh: 对Belikov来说，这证实了没有人拥有Tetris的家用主机版权。
cues.en: For Belikov, it was confirmation that no one had the home console rights to Tetris.

cues.zh: Belikov若完全无视Maxwell，那就太愚蠢了，即便他知道对方满嘴胡言。
cues.en: It would be foolish for Belikov to completely blow off Maxwell, even if he knew he was full of it.

cues.zh: 他们与俄罗斯的关系很关键，而且他们财力雄厚。
cues.en: Their connections to Russia were relevant, and they had deep pockets.

cues.zh: “如果那确实是Tetris的盗版拷贝，”Belikov说，“那么Mirrorsoft应该竞标家用主机版权。”
cues.en: "if it was indeed a pirated copy of Tetris," Belikov said, "then Mirrorsoft should make a bid for the home console rights."

cues.zh: 他还抛出了另一笔交易：ELORG将获得Maxwell公司几本参考书和百科全书的出版权。
cues.en: He threw in another deal as well: ELORG would receive publishing rights to several Maxwell Corporation reference books and encyclopedias.

cues.zh: 作为交换，Mirrorsoft获得了Tetris任何新权利的优先拒绝权。
cues.en: In exchange, Mirrorsoft was given a Right of First Refusal for any new rights to Tetris.

cues.zh: Maxwell对这个安排很满意，便回了家，自认为为Mirrorsoft推动了事情朝积极方向发展。
cues.en: Maxwell was satisfied with the arrangement and returned home, thinking he had moved things in a positive direction for Mirrorsoft.

cues.zh: 实际上，他已经妥协了一切。
cues.en: In reality, he had compromised everything.

cues.zh: 回到酒店房间，Robert Stein 仔细阅读了与 ELORG 原合同的修订条款。
cues.en: Back in his hotel room, Robert Stein read over the amendment to his original contract with ELORG.

cues.zh: 内容基本一样，只是增加了对逾期付款的严厉处罚。
cues.en: It was basically the same, plus some extreme penalties for late payments.

cues.zh: 拿到街机版权至关重要，为了得到它，Stein 不得不签署这份修订协议。
cues.en: Getting the arcade rights was crucial, and in order to get them, Stein had to sign the amendment.

cues.zh: 他签了字，第二天就返回了 ELORG。
cues.en: He signed it and returned to ELORG the next day.

cues.zh: 这件事解决后，谈判得以继续。
cues.en: With that out of the way, negotiations could continue.

cues.zh: 但 Belikov 声称 ELORG 还没准备好出售掌机版权。
cues.en: But Belikov claimed ELORG wasn't ready to sell the handheld rights.

cues.zh: 不过，街机版权是可以出售的。
cues.en: The arcade rights, however, were for sale.

cues.zh: 价格是：预付版税 15 万美元，期限六周。
cues.en: The cost: $150,000 for advanced royalty payments, with a six week deadline.

cues.zh: 这是一大笔钱，但至少 Stein 能避免 Tengen 和 Sega 街机版俄罗斯方块出现任何授权问题。
cues.en: It was a lot of money, but at least Stein would avoid any licensing issues for Tengen and Sega's arcade version of Tetris.

cues.zh: Stein回到家，心满意足。
cues.en: Stein returned home, feeling satisfied.

cues.zh: 但Stein在新修正案中漏掉了一个关键细节。
cues.en: But there was one crucial detail Stein missed in the new amendment.

cues.zh: Belikov加了一条关于计算机的定义，说计算机“由处理器、显示器、磁盘驱动器、键盘和操作系统组成”。
cues.en: Belikov added a definition for a computer, which said that a computer, "...consists of a processor, monitor, disk drive, keyboard, and operating system."

cues.zh: 由于文件被倒签了日期，这实际上剥夺了Stein自以为拥有的一切主机权利。
cues.en: Since the document was back dated, it effectively stripped away all the console rights Stein thought he owned.

cues.zh: 逾期付款的高额罚金，原来都只是障眼法。
cues.en: The large penalties for late payments had all been a distraction.

cues.zh: ELORG的俄罗斯人玩起了资本主义的游戏……而且赢了。
cues.en: The Russians at ELORG had played the game of capitalism... and won.

cues.zh: 会议结束后，Belikov打电话给Rogers，告诉他Kevin Maxwell和Mirrorsoft也想要Tetris的掌机版权。
cues.en: After his meetings, Belikov called Rogers to inform him that Kevin Maxwell and Mirrorsoft also wanted the handheld rights for Tetris.

cues.zh: “我出价拼不过Maxwell，但我能给你诚信，并承诺每盒卡带都付你钱，”Rogers说。
cues.en: "I can't outbid Maxwell, but I can give you honesty and promise to pay you for each cartridge," said Rogers.

cues.zh: 几天后，Rogers向ELORG提交了一份最终合同，并逐一过了一遍所有细节。
cues.en: Several days later, Rogers presented ELORG with a finalized contract and walked through every detail.

cues.zh: 事情正式敲定：Rogers和Nintendo拿下了俄罗斯方块在Game Boy上的掌机版权。
cues.en: It was official: Rogers and Nintendo secured the handheld rights to Tetris for the Game Boy.

cues.zh: 签完合同后，Belikov向Rogers提出一个提议：竞标俄罗斯方块的家用主机版权。
cues.en: After signing the contract, Belikov presented Rogers with an offer: make a bid on the home console rights to Tetris.

cues.zh: Rogers知道Nintendo会有兴趣。
cues.en: Rogers knew Nintendo would be interested.

cues.zh: “Nintendo的出价会压过任何竞争对手，”Rogers说。
cues.en: "Nintendo will outbid any competitor," Rogers said.

cues.zh: Belikov要求在三周内提交书面报价，随后会议就结束了。
cues.en: Belikov asked for an offer in writing within three weeks, and with that, the meeting was adjourned.

cues.zh: Rogers返回了日本。
cues.en: Rogers headed back to Japan.

cues.zh: 他时间紧迫，一刻也耽误不得。
cues.en: He had no time to spare.

cues.zh: 一回到日本，Henk Rogers就打电话给Nintendo of America的Minoru Arakawa，告知了这个消息。
cues.en: As soon as he got back to Japan, Henk Rogers phoned Minoru Arakawa at Nintendo of America with the news.

cues.zh: Nintendo不仅拿到了俄罗斯方块的掌机版权，而且由于合同上的问题，他们还有机会拿下家用主机版权。
cues.en: Nintendo not only had the handheld rights to Tetris, but due to contractual issues, they had a chance to snag the home console rights as well.

cues.zh: Arakawa把消息转达给了任天堂美国副总裁Howard Lincoln。
cues.en: Arakawa relayed the message to Nintendo of America Vice President Howard Lincoln.

cues.zh: Lincoln眼睛一亮。
cues.en: Lincoln's eyes lit up.

cues.zh: 这笔交易能给任天堂带来数百万的收益。
cues.en: This deal could make millions for Nintendo.

cues.zh: 这也能狠狠地报复Atari Games——这家任天堂的前授权商，如今正起诉他们索赔1亿美元。
cues.en: It would also be sweet revenge against Atari Games, a former Nintendo licensee that was now suing them for 100 million dollars.

cues.zh: 这起诉讼源于Atari Games对任天堂授权政策的不满。
cues.en: The suit stemmed from Atari Games' frustration with Nintendo's licensee policies.

cues.zh: 他们指控任天堂违反反垄断法并进行不公平竞争。
cues.en: They alleged anti-trust violations and unfair competition.

cues.zh: 与此同时，Atari Games通过其子公司Tengen发行了一批未授权游戏。
cues.en: At the same time, Atari games released a batch of unlicensed games under their subsidiary, Tengen.

cues.zh: 它们是Nintendo Entertainment System上最早的未授权游戏。
cues.en: They were the very first unlicensed games on the Nintendo Entertainment System.

cues.zh: Tengen即将发行的产品之一就是《俄罗斯方块》的主机版。
cues.en: One of Tengen's upcoming releases was the console version of Tetris.

cues.zh: 夺走Tengen的《俄罗斯方块》版权会让他们很受伤，Lincoln心里很清楚。
cues.en: Taking Tengen's rights to Tetris would hurt, and Lincoln knew it.

cues.zh: 于是他们派罗杰斯回莫斯科，正式提出报价。
cues.en: So they sent Rogers back to Moscow to make a formal offer.

cues.zh: 随行的是一位知名律师，此人曾在苏联工作过，俄语流利。
cues.en: With him was a high-profile attorney who had previously worked in the Soviet Union and was fluent in Russian.

cues.zh: 他们给ELORG的报价令人难以置信：
cues.en: Their offer to ELORG was incredible:

cues.zh: 五百万美元，有保障。
cues.en: $5,000,000, guaranteed.

cues.zh: 按照之前的承诺，贝利科夫联系了Mirrorsoft，询问优先购买权。
cues.en: As promised, Belikov contacted Mirrorsoft for Right of First Refusal.

cues.zh: 1989年3月15日，他给他们发了一封电传，限他们一天之内回复还价。
cues.en: On March 15th, 1989, he sent them a Telex, and gave them one day to respond with a counteroffer.

cues.zh: 没有收到任何回复，ELORG准备与任天堂签约。
cues.en: When nothing came back, ELORG was ready to sign the deal with Nintendo.

cues.zh: 由于涉及金额巨大，必须由任天堂的一位员工来签合同。
cues.en: Due to the enormous amount of money at stake, a Nintendo employee had to sign the contract.

cues.zh: 林肯和荒川亲自出马。
cues.en: Lincoln and Arakawa went themselves.

cues.zh: 他们秘密出行：一旦被Atari Games发现，协议就可能泡汤。
cues.en: They traveled in secret: any chance of Atari Games finding out could jeopardize the agreement.

cues.zh: 他们告诉任天堂美国的员工说要去日本，然后动身飞往莫斯科。
cues.en: They told Nintendo of America employees they were traveling to Japan, and took off for Moscow.

cues.zh: 他们抵达后，谈判继续进行。
cues.en: Negotiations continued when they arrived.

cues.zh: 林肯确信雅达利游戏公司会来找他们麻烦。
cues.en: Lincoln was sure Atari Games would come after them.

cues.zh: 他想加入一项条款，规定俄方将在任何诉讼中帮助维护他们的权利。
cues.en: He wanted a clause stating that the Russians would help defend their rights in any litigation.

cues.zh: 林肯还建议向阿列克谢·帕基特诺夫支付版税，以奖励他创造了这款游戏。
cues.en: Lincoln also suggested royalty payments to Alexey Pajitnov for creating the game.

cues.zh: 别利科夫觉得这个建议……不合适。
cues.en: Belikov found the suggestion... inappropriate.

cues.zh: 帕基特诺夫是在公司上班时间做出这款游戏的。
cues.en: Pajitnov had made the game on company time.

cues.zh: 它属于国家。
cues.en: It belonged to the state.

cues.zh: 别利科夫建议由ELORG来生产卡带。
cues.en: Belikov suggested that ELORG could make the cartridges.

cues.zh: 他们甚至询问过能否生产自己的任天堂娱乐系统版本。
cues.en: They even inquired about making their own version of the Nintendo Entertainment System.

cues.zh: 任天堂拒绝了。
cues.en: Nintendo declined.

cues.zh: 在谈判的最后阶段，Mirrorsoft的吉姆·麦科诺基终于把电传消息回复给了ELORG。
cues.en: During the final stage of negotiations, Jim Mackonochie of Mirrorsoft finally returned the Telex message to ELORG.

cues.zh: 在麦科诺基看来，Mirrorsoft已经拥有了主机版权。
cues.en: As far as Mackonochie was concerned, Mirrorsoft already had the console rights.

cues.zh: ELORG 肯定搞错了。
cues.en: ELORG must be mistaken.

cues.zh: 这正是 ELORG 想听到的，1989 年 3 月 22 日，任天堂与 ELORG 签署了俄罗斯方块家用主机版权协议。
cues.en: That was all ELORG needed to hear, and on March 22nd, 1989, Nintendo and ELORG signed an agreement for the home console rights to Tetris.

cues.zh: 同一天，Belikov 又给 Mirrorsoft 和 Robert Stein 发了一封电传。
cues.en: That same day, Belikov fired off another Telex to Mirrorsoft and Robert Stein.

cues.zh: 俄罗斯方块的家用主机版权和掌机版权已不再可获取。
cues.en: The home console rights and handheld rights to Tetris were no longer available.

cues.zh: 它们归任天堂所有。
cues.en: They belonged to Nintendo.

cues.zh: Robert Stein 目瞪口呆。
cues.en: Robert Stein was dumbfounded.

cues.zh: “我太专注于得到我想要的东西，以至于忘了去留意他们想要什么，”他说。
cues.en: "I was so focused on getting what I wanted, that I forgot about watching what they wanted," he said.

cues.zh: 他觉得自己是撒谎、背后捅刀和欺骗的受害者。
cues.en: He felt he was the victim of lying, backstabbing and cheating.

cues.zh: 他指控 Henk Rogers 在修订合同上与俄罗斯人串通。
cues.en: He accused Henk Rogers of colluding with the Russians on the amended contract.

cues.zh: 他还认为 Kevin Maxwell 与 Belikov 的会面把所有人都坑了。
cues.en: He also argued that Kevin Maxwell's meeting with Belikov had screwed everyone over.

cues.zh: “他是在埋葬我，埋葬我们所有人，”Stein 说。
cues.en: "He was burying me, burying us all," Stein said.

cues.zh: 至少还有点小小的安慰奖：
cues.en: At least there was a small consolation prize:

cues.zh: Stein 仍然拥有《俄罗斯方块》的家用电脑和街机版权。
cues.en: Stein still had the home computer and arcade rights to Tetris.

cues.zh: Kevin Maxwell 听到这个消息后勃然大怒。
cues.en: Kevin Maxwell was furious when he heard the news.

cues.zh: “你们现在两次严重违反了我们与你们的协议，”他在给 ELORG 的回电中说道。
cues.en: "You are now in grave breach twice over of our agreements with you," he said in a reply Telex to ELORG.

cues.zh: 他还威胁要让苏联当局介入。
cues.en: He also threatened to get Soviet authorities involved.

cues.zh: 他不是在虚张声势；
cues.en: He wasn't bluffing;

cues.zh: 俄罗斯政府质询了 Nikoli Belikov；
cues.en: the Russian government questioned Nikoli Belikov;

cues.zh: 他们搜查了他的文件。
cues.en: they searched his files.

cues.zh: 但 Belikov 坚持立场，并向任天堂保证他们会履行承诺。
cues.en: But Belikov stood his ground, and assured Nintendo that they would honor their commitment.

cues.zh: 当 Kevin Maxwell 把《俄罗斯方块》的消息告诉父亲时，据说他“彻底暴怒了”。
cues.en: When Kevin Maxwell told his father the news about Tetris, he reportedly, quote, "went apeshit."

cues.zh: Robert Maxwell 一路把怒火发到了米哈伊尔·戈尔巴乔夫那里，后者当时已是苏联总书记。
cues.en: Robert Maxwell took his anger all the way to Mikhail Gorbachev, now general secretary of the Soviet Union.

cues.zh: 戈尔巴乔夫手头有更重要的事要处理。
cues.en: Gorbachev had more important matters at hand.

cues.zh: 他的国家濒临崩溃。
cues.en: His country was on the verge of collapse.

cues.zh: “你不用再担心那家日本公司了，”戈尔巴乔夫对麦克斯韦说。
cues.en: "You should no longer worry about the Japanese company," Gorbachev told Maxwell.

cues.zh: 就这样，Mirrorsoft 放弃了俄罗斯方块之争。
cues.en: And with that, Mirrorsoft gave up the fight for Tetris.

cues.zh: 1989年3月31日，Atari Games 总裁中岛英之收到了来自任天堂美国公司 Howard Lincoln 的一封令人意外的传真。
cues.en: On March 31st, 1989, president Hideyuki Nakajima of Atari Games received a surprising fax from Howard Lincoln, of Nintendo of America.

cues.zh: 这是一份停止令，命令他们停止“为 NES 或任何其他家用系统进一步制造、宣传、推广、要约销售或销售俄罗斯方块”。
cues.en: It was a Cease & Desist, ordering them to halt from, "any further manufacture, advertisement, promotion, offer for sale, or sale of Tetris for the NES, or any other home system."

cues.zh: 版权现在归任天堂所有。
cues.en: The rights now belonged to Nintendo.

cues.zh: “我们知道我们牢牢拿捏住了那帮混蛋，”Lincoln 说。
cues.en: "We knew we had those bastards by the balls," said Lincoln.

cues.zh: 1989年4月6日，任天堂发布官方新闻稿，宣布计划于当年夏天在 NES 上发行俄罗斯方块。
cues.en: On April 6th, 1989, Nintendo sent out an official press release, announcing plans to release Tetris that summer on the NES.

cues.zh: 第二天，Atari Games 通过其子公司 Tengen 给任天堂发了一封回信。
cues.en: The next day, Atari Games, via their subsidiary Tengen, sent a reply to Nintendo.

cues.zh: “我们已收到贵方来信……坦白说，我们非常困惑。
cues.en: "We are in receipt of your letter....and quite frankly are quite confused.

cues.zh: 正如任天堂自去年以来所知，Tengen 已于 1988 年初获得游戏《俄罗斯方块》的全部 NES 版权。
cues.en: As Nintendo has known since last year, Tengen received all NES rights to the game 'Tetris' in early 1988.

cues.zh: 在 Tengen 看来，这些权利清晰明确、毫无疑义……”
cues.en: These rights are, in Tengen's view, clear and unequivocal..."

cues.zh: 但 Atari Games 慌了。
cues.en: But Atari Games was panicking.

cues.zh: 一周后，他们为自己版本的《俄罗斯方块》提交了版权申请。
cues.en: A week later, they filed a copyright application for their version of Tetris.

cues.zh: 4 月 18 日，他们起诉任天堂侵犯了其《俄罗斯方块》授权协议。
cues.en: On April 18th, they sued Nintendo for infringing on their licensing deal for Tetris.

cues.zh: 几乎一切都悬于一线。
cues.en: Almost everything was at stake.

cues.zh: Atari Games 预计《俄罗斯方块》会大获成功，足以击破任天堂巨头的护盾。
cues.en: Atari Games anticipated Tetris to be a colossal hit that would break the shields of the Nintendo juggernaut.

cues.zh: 他们指派资深程序员 Ed Logg 从零开始编写 NES 版本；
cues.en: They assigned veteran programmer Ed Logg to program the NES version from the ground up;

cues.zh: 他们在营销上投入了大量资金；
cues.en: they spent a substantial amount of money on marketing;

cues.zh: 他们在《今日美国》上买下整版广告；
cues.en: they took out a full-page ad in USA Today;

cues.zh: 他们生产了 30 万份《俄罗斯方块》；
cues.en: they produced 300,000 copies of Tetris;

cues.zh: 他们甚至在纽约市的 Russian Tea Room 举办了盛大的发布派对。
cues.en: they even held a huge launch party at the Russian Tea Room in New York City.

cues.zh: 1989年5月17日，正值法律纠纷期间，Tengen在任天堂娱乐系统上发布了俄罗斯方块。
cues.en: On May 17th, 1989, in the midst of their legal battles, Tengen released Tetris on the Nintendo Entertainment System.

cues.zh: 不出所料，游戏迅速售罄，几周内卖出了15万份。
cues.en: As expected, it flew off the shelves, selling 150,000 copies within weeks.

cues.zh: 与此同时，Howard Lincoln带着一队律师返回莫斯科，为即将到来的战斗做准备。
cues.en: Meanwhile, Howard Lincoln headed back to Moscow with a team of lawyers to prepare for the upcoming battle.

cues.zh: 他们尽可能多地约谈了相关人员：
cues.en: They interviewed everyone they could:

cues.zh: Alexey Pajitnov；
cues.en: Alexey Pajitnov;

cues.zh: Nikoli Belikov；
cues.en: Nikoli Belikov;

cues.zh: 以及ELORG和俄罗斯科学院的员工。
cues.en: and employees of ELORG and the Russian Academy of Sciences.

cues.zh: 他们仔细梳理了Robert Stein与ELORG之间每一份合同的副本。
cues.en: They combed over every copy of the contracts between Robert Stein and ELORG.

cues.zh: 1989年6月15日，Tengen和任天堂在加利福尼亚北区美国联邦地区法院展开辩论。
cues.en: On June 15th, 1989, Tengen and Nintendo opened their arguments in the US District Court of Northern, California.

cues.zh: 主审此案的是Fern Smith法官，她也是另一起涉及Tengen未经授权游戏的诉讼案的负责法官。
cues.en: Presiding over the case was Judge Fern Smith, the same judge in charge of their other lawsuit dealing with the unlicensed Tengen games.

cues.zh: Nintendo和Atari Games双方都申请了初步禁令，试图阻止对方销售其版本的Tetris。
cues.en: Both Nintendo and Atari Games filed preliminary injunctions, which would prevent the other from selling their version of Tetris.

cues.zh: Atari Games辩称，他们从Mirrorsoft获得的授权是有效的，而俄罗斯人是在两头收钱。
cues.en: Atari Games argued that their license from Mirrorsoft was valid, and that the Russians were double-dipping.

cues.zh: Nintendo则主张，俄罗斯人从未打算向Mirrorsoft出售除家用电脑版权之外的任何权利。
cues.en: Nintendo argued that the Russians never intended to sell anything other than the home computer rights to Mirrorsoft.

cues.zh: 但决定性证据是那份修订后的合同，其中对家用电脑系统作出了定义。
cues.en: But the Smoking Gun was the amended contract, which defined a home computer system.

cues.zh: NES显然不符合那一定义。
cues.en: The NES definitely did not match that definition.

cues.zh: 6月22日，Fern Smith法官作出了裁决。
cues.en: On June 22nd, Judge Fern Smith reached her decision.

cues.zh: 她批准了Nintendo的初步禁令，禁止Atari Games销售其版本的Tetris。
cues.en: She granted Nintendo a preliminary injunction, barring Atari Games from selling their version of Tetris.

cues.zh: 庭审定于当年11月晚些时候进行。
cues.en: The trial was scheduled for later that year in November.

cues.zh: 这对Atari Games是一次沉重打击。
cues.en: It was a huge blow to Atari Games.

cues.zh: 那时，最初30万份游戏几乎卖出了一半，让他们仓库里堆满了游戏。
cues.en: By then, almost half of the initial 300,000 copies had been sold, leaving them with a warehouse full of games.

cues.zh: 消费者得知消息后，纷纷抢购自己的那一份。
cues.en: When consumers heard the news, people rushed to snag their own copy.

cues.zh: 许多人从租赁店借了游戏后就干脆留下，乐意支付替换费。
cues.en: Many who borrowed the game from rental stores simply kept it, happily paying the replacement fee.

cues.zh: 1989年7月31日，任天堂在北美推出了Game Boy，并捆绑销售一份Tetris。
cues.en: On July 31st, 1989, Nintendo unleashed the Game Boy in North America, bundled with a copy of Tetris.

cues.zh: 任天堂觉得他们的案子有明确且有力的证据。
cues.en: Nintendo felt their case had clear and compelling evidence.

cues.zh: 他们请求法官Fern Smith作出简易判决，这样可以在审判开始前就结案。
cues.en: They asked Judge Fern Smith for a summary judgment, which would end the trial before it began.

cues.zh: 出乎他们意料的是，法官Fern Smith同意了。
cues.en: To their surprise, Judge Fern Smith agreed.

cues.zh: 1989年11月13日，她裁定任天堂拥有Tetris的家用主机版权。
cues.en: On November 13th, 1989, she ruled that Nintendo owned the home console rights to Tetris.

cues.zh: Atari Games宣布将提起上诉，但后来决定放弃。
cues.en: Atari Games announced they would appeal, but later decided against it.

cues.zh: 他们销毁了所有剩余的俄罗斯方块库存副本。
cues.en: They destroyed all of their remaining warehoused copies of Tetris.

cues.zh: 同月，任天堂在 NES 上发布了自己的俄罗斯方块版本。
cues.en: That same month, Nintendo released their version of Tetris on the NES.

cues.zh: 这款游戏最终卖出了超过 500 万份。
cues.en: It would go on to sell more than 5 million copies.

cues.zh: 这场围绕这款令人上瘾的俄罗斯益智游戏的争夺战终于结束了。
cues.en: The battle for the addictive Russian puzzle game was finally over.

cues.zh: Henk Rogers 的预测是对的：俄罗斯方块会让 Game Boy 吸引所有人。
cues.en: Henk Rogers' prediction that Tetris would make the Game Boy appeal to everyone was correct.

cues.zh: 到 2003 年，任天堂售出了超过 1.18 亿台 Game Boy。
cues.en: By 2003, Nintendo sold over 118 million Game Boys.

cues.zh: 其中 3500 万台是随俄罗斯方块捆绑销售的。
cues.en: 35 million of them were bundled with Tetris.

cues.zh: 虽然任天堂是明显的赢家，但几乎所有参与其中的人都赚到了钱：Robert Stein、Spectrum HoloByte、Mirrorsoft、Henk Rogers、ELORG 和 Atari Games。
cues.en: Although Nintendo emerged as the clear victors, just about everyone involved: Robert Stein, Spectrum HoloByte, Mirrorsoft, Henk Rogers, ELORG, and Atari Games made money on Tetris.

cues.zh: 所有人，也就是说，除了它的创造者：Alexey Pajitnov。
cues.en: Everyone, that is, except its creator: Alexey Pajitnov.

cues.zh: 到 1989 年，他从俄罗斯方块中一分钱都没拿到，仍然在俄罗斯科学院工作。
cues.en: By 1989, he had collected nothing from Tetris, and was still working at the Russian Academy of Sciences.

cues.zh: 他已婚，有两个孩子。
cues.en: He was married with two children.

cues.zh: 但1991年，他的命运发生了转变。
cues.en: But in 1991, his fortunes changed.

cues.zh: Henk Rogers决心帮助他的朋友。
cues.en: Henk Rogers was determined to help his friend.

cues.zh: 他帮助Pajitnov及其家人移民到西雅图地区，Pajitnov在那里创办了自己的软件公司。
cues.en: He helped Pajitnov and his family immigrate to the Seattle area, where Pajitnov founded his own software company.

cues.zh: 1995年，俄罗斯方块的版权到期，这让Pajitnov终于有机会从他的创作中获得收益。
cues.en: In 1995, the rights to Tetris expired, which gave Pajitnov the opportunity to finally cash in on his creation.

cues.zh: 那时，ELORG已是一家私营公司，仍由Nikoli Belikov领导。
cues.en: By that point, ELORG was a private company, still under the direction of Nikoli Belikov.

cues.zh: ELORG购买了俄罗斯方块50%的版权。
cues.en: ELORG purchased 50% of the rights to Tetris.

cues.zh: Rogers和Pajitnov合作成立了俄罗斯方块公司，并购买了另外一半版权。
cues.en: Rogers and Pajitnov partnered up and formed The Tetris Company, and purchased the other half.

cues.zh: 经过漫长的13年，Alexey Pajitnov终于拿到了他游戏的版税。
cues.en: After 13 long years, Alexey Pajitnov finally received royalty payments for his game.

cues.zh: 时至今日，俄罗斯方块系列已售出超过1.7亿份游戏，成为有史以来第七畅销的电子游戏系列。
